# The Harvest, Act 1: voice guide for every line the player reads

## Who is talking
The player character is the pilot of the small ship *Outrider*: a bearded, middle-aged human repair pilot taken from a spacewalk above Earth by a living alien harvester ship. Narration is HIS thoughts, first person, present tense ("A cracked pod. Still warm."). He is dry, curious, warm and quietly funny under pressure: a working man who fixes things, not a poet and not a horror narrator.

## The feel: King's Quest V and VI
A storybook adventure. Wonder sits next to danger. Most clicks reward the player with a short, pleasing observation or a small joke; real menace is saved for the moments that matter (the Curator, the hunters, deaths). The world can be strange and a bit gross, but the writing is never relentlessly grim: at most one dark image per line, little gore, no wallowing in decay, corpses or despair.

## Length (explorers click everything: keep it quick)
- LOOK: 1 to 2 sentences, aim under 140 characters; up to about 220 only for real story beats or puzzle clues.
- HAND / TALK / MOVE flavour: 1 sentence, under about 110 characters.
- Item descriptions: 1 to 2 sentences, under about 160.
- Lines in a random pool ("random"): under about 90 each, and varied.
- Hints ("hint"): plain advice to the player (second person is fine here, it's the game helping), 1 to 2 sentences, under about 160.
- Death screens ("death screen"): a Sierra-style wry epitaph in the game's own voice; "you" is fine here. 1 to 2 sentences, under about 170, ideally with a gentle nudge about what to do differently.
- Patrol warnings, meter warnings and other system lines ("...message"): short, clear, urgent. One sentence where possible.

## Keep, always
- Every puzzle clue and fact: item names, colors, shapes, the glyph descriptions, directions, counts, which thing does what, warnings that prevent a death, noise warnings, "it needs X" information. If cutting would lose a clue, keep the clue and cut around it.
- Names (Keth-Vari, the Curator, the Vesk, Vera, the Archivist, the Choir, LUMEN-7, Outrider) and capitalised verbs (LOOK, HAND, MOVE, TALK).
- Words spoken by other characters (in quotes or dialogue prompts): keep their voice and meaning; you may trim them.
- First person for his narration (no "you" addressed to the player outside hints and death screens).

## Cut
- Purple prose and stacked adjectives; repeating what another line of the same object already said.
- Stock "AI" habits: lists of three adjectives, "it's not X, it's Y", "a testament to", "whispers of", "echoes of", "a symphony of", em-dash asides, a rhetorical question in every line, portentous one-word closing sentences ("Alive." "Waiting.").
- The same atmosphere beat over and over (the ship humming, the walls breathing, the smell of chemicals): say it once where it matters.

## Humour
Roughly one flavour line in three gets a light, character-driven joke: dry understatement, a tired pilot's practicality, an Earth comparison. No memes, no modern slang, no winking at the player about being in a game.

## Process
Lines are grouped by object ("where" says which, and which verb). Read an object's lines together so they don't repeat each other. If a line is already short and good, return it unchanged.

lines.The scratches on the walls look delibera: The scratches on the walls look deliberate. Examine them more closely.

lines.The Gut's door is far to the west, behin: The Gut's door is far west, behind a Choir quarantine seal; the seal's lever is far east. Your map is north-up: count your turns.
lines.The map is north-up and has no 'you are: The map is north-up with no 'you are here': count your turns. Left is west, right is east. Go east to the lever first, then back west. The big skull is bad air (wear the helmet); small skulls are purge ducts.

lines.An airlock bay. Your ship might have bee: An airlock bay. Look around: the clamps, the viewport, the override panel.
lines.The docking clamps are empty — your ship: The docking clamps are empty: your ship is gone. Check the suit locker and the viewport.

lines.I climb back into my cracked pod, pull m: I climb back into my pod, knees up, and go limp: just another specimen. Hold still.
lines.I climb back into my cracked pod and cur: I curl up in my pod. The clicking passes along the walkway, hesitates, and fades.
lines.The pod hangs open, drained of fluid. My: The pod hangs open and drained, my outline pressed into the residue, arms crossed like a pharaoh. A specimen tag dangles from the frame.
lines.I carefully snap off a curved shard of p: I snap a curved shard off the broken edge: some alien composite, light and razor-sharp. A crude tool, but a tool.
lines.I whisper to myself, staring at the empt: "How long was I in there?" The pod answers with a drip.

lines.A shallow channel cut into the floor, fe: A shallow floor channel draining slowly to the ship's recyclers. Amber stasis fluid pools here.
lines.I cup my hands and try to scoop up the a: The fluid is too thick to scoop and slips through my fingers. I need a container; the processing lab down the corridor might have one.
lines.The channel is mostly drained now. A thi: The channel is mostly drained now. Just an amber film, nothing worth collecting.
lines.I dip the sample jar into the amber flui: I dip the jar into the amber fluid. It fills fast and seals itself with a soft click.
lines.I listen to the fluid gurgling into the: The fluid gurgles into the drain in a slow pulse, like breathing.
lines.Rows of intact pods stretching into the: Rows of intact pods rising into the shadows. A few still glow.
lines.Rows of hexagonal pods stretch up into t: Pods climb into the dark, specimens from dozens of worlds in amber. A few still pulse with life. All too high to reach.
lines.I tap on the nearest pod's surface. The: I tap the nearest pod. The fluid swirls; the creature inside doesn't stir.
lines.\"Can you hear me?\" I murmur, pressing: "Can you hear me?" The creature inside doesn't stir. Maybe that's a mercy.
lines.A section of walkway railing has been to: A stretch of railing is torn away over the drainage pit. The cataloguer's platform has a solid railing on the far side.
lines.The walkway railing is torn apart here,: Twisted railing over a gap, the pit dark below. Too wide to jump. But the far railing is solid: something thrown across to catch on it, with me holding the other end...
lines.My grappling line spans the gap, the hoo: My grappling line spans the gap, hook bitten into the far railing. I can cross whenever I like.
lines.I fall into the drainage pit, tumbling t: I tumble into the pit. The last thing I see is amber fluid closing over my face.
lines.The Choir thank you for returning yourse: The Choir thank you for returning yourself to the recycling system. Next time, bring something to hold on to.
lines.I go hand over hand along my line above: Hand over hand above the pit. No easier the second time, but I know it holds.
lines.I swing the hook in a widening circle an: I swing the hook and let it fly. It clangs, slides, and bites the far railing. I lash my end to the stump here. It sags in the middle. It'll hold. Probably.
lines.I could tie one end here, but the other: I could tie one end here, but the far end needs something to catch on. Thrown loose, the strap would just flop into the pit.
lines.I could throw the hook across, but then: I could throw the hook across, but with nothing tied to it I'd just be throwing away a good hook.
lines.The shard is sharp, but sharp won't get: Sharp won't get me across. I need something that reaches the far railing and holds on.
lines.The tendril is barely a foot long and sl: The tendril is a foot long and slick. I'd need something much longer that can catch on the far railing.
The gap is too wide to walk across. I need a safe way to the other side.
lines.My line, the hook bitten deep into the f: My line, hooked on the far railing and lashed on this side. HAND it to climb across.

lines.A spider-legged machine perched among th: A spider-legged machine among the pods, cataloguing specimens.
lines.The cataloguer is still across the pit,: The cataloguer is across the pit, too far to read its displays. My line is rigged: HAND it to climb across.
lines.A biomechanical spider-drone clings to t: A spider-drone on the far wall, scanning specimens. Its jars' data plates show alien script beside numbers, but it's across the gap, too far to read.
lines.Now that I'm close, I can read the displ: Up close, the displays under the jars all show the same four alien characters, always in the same order. I learn their shapes by heart. A section code, probably.
lines.I've already memorized the four characte: I've already memorized the four characters on the specimen displays. No harm in looking again.
lines.I stretch toward the cataloguer, but it': The cataloguer is across the gap. Out of reach until I find a way over.
lines.A small tag hanging from my pod's frame,: A small tag hanging from my pod's frame, etched with alien notation.

lines.I mouth the alien numerals on the tag ho: I try mouthing the alien numerals on the tag. Human throats weren't built for this.
lines.A walkway runs between the pod racks. Th: A walkway between the pod racks. The metal is warm and slightly flexible.

lines.The railing flexes slightly under my gri: The railing flexes under my grip like a thick branch. Sturdy, and a little too warm.
lines.A passage leading to Containment Corrido: A passage leading to the Containment Corridor.
lines.A dark archway between the pod racks lea: A dark archway between the pod racks, faint orange light flickering beyond.
lines.I slip through the archway between tower: I slip through the archway into the humming corridor.
lines.I trail my fingers along the archway's e: The archway's edge is warm and damp, like the inside of a mouth. I wipe my hand on my tunic.
lines.I call out into the corridor beyond. My: I call into the corridor. My voice comes back flat, as if something swallowed it.
lines.Specimen 7319-101: a Velith Ammonite — a: Specimen 7319-101: a Velith Ammonite, a deep-ocean cephalopod with a coiled nautilus shell and dozens of tentacles.
lines.The Velith Ammonite floats in the amber: Part octopus, part nautilus, its skin still shifting color. The green display below scrolls glyphs beside a specimen number.
lines.The glass is warm to the touch and faint: The glass is warm and hums. The shell turns a fraction in the fluid. I'd like to think that was the ship.
I mutter at the shell. Its chambers glow one after another, like a sequence trying to answer.
lines.Specimen 7319-102: a Kethrani Weaver — a: Specimen 7319-102: a Kethrani Weaver, a huge eight-legged arachnoid predator with an armored carapace and bone-crushing mandibles.
lines.The Kethrani Weaver fills the center tan: The Weaver fills the center tank, bigger than I am, all legs and mandibles. The green display scrolls glyphs beside a specimen number. I'm glad I never visited.
I press my palm to the glass. A leg twitches and the mandibles click once. I take my palm back.
lines.\"What happened to you?\" I whisper. The: "What happened to you?" Hundreds of dark facets stare back, each holding a tiny copy of my face.
lines.Specimen 7319-103: a Neural Orchid — an: Specimen 7319-103: a Neural Orchid, an alien plant with burgundy petals and thick root tendrils, preserved in golden fluid.
lines.Not an animal. A plant. Or something tha: Burgundy petals, and roots curling through the fluid like searching fingers. The green display scrolls a specimen number. The petals seem to open as I watch.
lines.I tap the glass. The orchid's root tendr: I tap the glass. The roots drift toward my finger and the petals spread, almost hungrily. It would collect me back if it could.
lines.\"You're beautiful,\" I whisper to the o: "You're beautiful," I whisper. The outer petals open, very slightly, toward my voice.
lines.I keep talking to it, low and kind, the: I keep talking, low and kind, like to a nervous dog. The petals unfurl further. Something golden glows in its throat.
lines.\"Go on,\" I whisper. The orchid opens a: "Go on." It breathes out one glowing spore, which drifts through the glass and sinks into my hand, warm as a coal. I feel, absurdly, encouraged.
lines.Three glowing teal screens below the tan: Three glowing teal screens below the tanks, scrolling alien glyphs and specimen numbers.
lines.The same four characters, in the same or: The names change from tank to tank, but these four characters never do, always in the same order. A code, probably. I commit the shapes to memory.
The same four characters, in the same order. I have them by heart.
The same four characters on every tank, in the same order. They must unlock something on this ship.
lines.I try to sound out the four characters o: I try to sound out the four characters. My mouth doesn't make those shapes.
lines.A large green screen showing a detailed: A large green screen showing an alien organism diagram with alien annotations.
lines.The main screen shows a detailed biologi: A spiny, many-limbed organism drawn in green lines, framed by curling alien script. The screen is locked to this display.
lines.The screen has changed. It now cycles th: The screen cycles processing schedules. The current harvest: one yellow star, eight planets, the third from the sun. Earth. The ship is already in orbit. Red script at the bottom: the security console's override is armed.
lines.The processing records keep cycling. Ear: Earth is still on the harvesting schedule. I have to stop this ship, or warn someone. Red script at the bottom: the security console's override is armed.
lines.I touch the screen surface. It ripples l: The screen ripples like warm, wet skin. Living tissue, not a monitor.
lines.A small keypad of eight bio-organic keys: Eight bio-organic keys, each etched with an alien character like those around the ship. It wants four, in the right order.
lines.The keypad glows a steady green — access: The keypad glows a steady green: access granted. The terminal is unlocked.
lines.The keypad is already showing green — th: The keypad is already green and the terminal unlocked. No need to enter the code again.
lines.\"Open sesame.\" The keypad, which has n: "Open sesame." The keypad, which has never heard of Ali Baba, stays shut.
lines.A small monitor showing processing statu: A small monitor showing processing status and system diagnostics.
lines.A small monitor displaying what looks li: A green schematic of pathways and nodes, locked to this diagnostic view.
lines.With the terminal unlocked, this monitor: A processing queue now. One entry, 'XY-97-A | C44', reads 'INTAKE PENDING'. That's my tag. Next on my schedule: Neural Integration. No thank you.
lines.The monitor's surface is the same biolum: The same warm, damp membrane as the main screen. The keypad controls it.
lines.I glare at the processing queue. The pro: I glare at the processing queue. The queue, being a list, glares back without blinking.
lines.A small monitor showing specimen classif: A small monitor showing specimen classification records.
lines.Another small monitor, this one showing: Rows of alien characters and numbers: a specimen registry, locked behind the same code as the main terminal.
lines.The registry shows every species the Con: Under 'SOL-3', seventeen Earth species: Felis catus, Canis familiaris, Homo sapiens... They've been sampling us for years. The black cat in the corridor escaped, like me.
lines.I can't interact with this display direc: I can't work this display directly. The keypad controls all the terminal's screens.
lines.\"Show me what you've got,\" I tell the: "Show me what you've got." What it's got is a lock symbol. Fair enough.
lines.I hold the specimen tag up to the regist: The registry reads my tag: XY-97-A, C44, Homo sapiens, SOL-3. 'Unusual cognitive resistance. Recommend accelerated processing.' I'm flattered, and terrified.
lines.Long tables with organic restraints, des: Long tables with organic restraints, made for specimens much bigger than me.
lines.Two examination tables dominate the room: Two examination tables, their organic clamps sized for things far larger than a man. They've seen a lot of use.
lines.I climb onto the nearest table. Standing: I touch the restraints and they twitch, sensing a meal of biomass. I step back quickly.
lines.I mutter to myself, studying the stained: "Whatever they did here, they did it to a lot of us."
lines.A rack of alien surgical tools — curved: A rack of alien surgical tools: curved bone-like instruments, probes and extractors.
lines.Surgical instruments arranged with obses: Grown surgical tools, laid out with obsessive care. Most are made for bigger hands than mine, but a small probe near the bottom looks manageable.
lines.I reach for the smallest instrument, a p: I take the smallest probe, fine-tipped and flexible. Good for locks, screws and delicate mechanisms.
lines.I name each tool under my breath, trying: None of these tools match any surgery I know, which is not reassuring.
lines.Dozens of sealed jars holding biological: Sealed jars of tissue and organs. I spot a heart and an eye and stop looking. One jar on the lower shelf is empty, its seal cracked open.
Sealed jars of tissue and organs. I spot a heart and an eye and stop looking.
lines.Most of the jars are sealed tight with b: One jar on the lower shelf is cracked open, its contents dried to a crust. I pry it free. The jar itself is intact: good for collecting samples.
lines.I reach toward the jars but pull back. T: I reach toward the jars and pull back. Their contents shift when my shadow falls on them.
lines.I lean close and whisper. The pale thing: I whisper to the nearest jar. The pale thing inside twitches. I stop whispering.
lines.Screens cycling through biological data: Screens cycling through biological data and procedures.
lines.Not with the hunter drone hanging right: Not with the hunter drone hanging right beside it. I'll leave the lab and come back when it's gone.
lines.I reach for the terminal. The lens snaps: I reach for the terminal. The drone's lens snaps onto me.
lines.The hunter drone was waiting for exactly: The drone was waiting for exactly that. It pins you to the terminal until the Curator arrives. Next time, leave the lab and let it lose interest.
lines.The screens cycle through processing rou: The screens cycle through intake, classification, preservation, disposal. Below them, a terminal with an alien keypad. I lean in...
lines.A large holographic screen showing detai: A large holographic screen showing anatomical cross-sections.
Cross-sections of... me. A human nervous system in green lines, the pain receptors picked out in red. Thorough.
lines.I study the holographic display. More sp: Dozens more species, each mapped in detail. My entry carries the same symbol as the pod labels. Catalogued.
lines.\"I'm not just a number,\" I mutter at t: "I'm not just a number." The hologram flips to a note: talking to objects is a 'common stress response in specimen 7G.'
lines.Thick straps bolted to the examination t: Thick straps, worn smooth. The buckles fit something far bigger, but new holes are punched in my size. They're built to take a lot of weight.
lines.One strap hangs severed where I cut it f: One strap hangs severed where I cut it free. The rest can stay for the next guest.
lines.I test the straps. They're impossibly st: Impossibly strong. I won't tear one loose by hand. I need something that cuts this stuff.
lines.I slide the probe's needle-fine edge und: I slip the probe's edge under a strap at the bolt. Choir tool, Choir material: it parts like wet paper. A long strap comes free, buckle and all, strong enough to hold me.
lines.I saw at a strap with the glass shard. T: The glass shard skates across the strap without a mark. I need a proper cutting tool, one made for this ship's materials.
lines.\"Who did they keep here?\" I whisper. T: "Who did they keep here?" The straps don't say. The holes punched in my size say plenty.
lines.Deep scratches and dark stains on the la: Deep scratches and dark stains on the lab floor. Something was dragged across here recently.
lines.Deep gouges scored into the lab floor, t: Claw gouges leading to the examination tables, dark stains beside them. They weren't here before. Something was processed while I was out.
lines.I trace the grooves with my fingers. Fiv: Five parallel grooves under my fingers. Claws, or fingers, and whoever made them didn't want to go.
lines.There's nothing to say to claw marks. Bu: Claw marks don't make conversation. Their message is clear enough anyway: don't get caught.
lines.A patch of bioluminescent growth that ha: A patch of glowing growth that has spread across the lab wall since I was last here.
lines.A patch of bioluminescent growth spreads: Glowing growth spreads where the wall was damaged. The ship is healing itself. I'm not in a ship so much as inside something.
lines.The growth is warm and slightly damp. It: Warm and damp. It flinches at my touch, glows brighter, then settles. Disgusting, and I can't stop poking it.
It flinches and glows. I could cut it with the glass shard, but that might rouse the ship's immune system, and whatever patrols the deck.
lines.I murmur to the organic growth. It pulse: I murmur to the growth. It pulses back, or it was going to pulse anyway. Hard to tell with a living ship.
lines.I slice into the growth with the glass s: I slice the growth with the shard. Beneath, scratched in a shaking human hand: "HARVEST. THEY TAKE EVERYTHING. FIND THE VENTS." The growth closes over it again.
lines.A large open archway at the back of the: A wide archway at the back of the lab leads to the containment corridor. Orange light flickers beyond.
lines.I pass under the archway and back into t: I pass under the archway into the containment corridor.
lines.I press my palm against the doorframe. I: The doorframe contracts slightly under my palm. The ship knows I'm here.
lines.The corridor beyond echoes with the ship: Out in the corridor I at least have choices about where to go.
lines.A hunter drone hangs beside the terminal: A hunter drone hangs by the terminal, lens sweeping, waiting for whoever tripped the alarm. Touch nothing near it. Leave the lab and let it lose interest.
lines.The hunter drone pins you to the floor i: The hunter drone pins you to the floor in a blink and hums until the Curator arrives. Next time, leave the lab and let it lose interest.
lines.Organic conduits pulse with green fluid: Overhead conduits pulse with green fluid. The ship's veins, more or less.
lines.The conduits are warm and faintly pulsin: Warm, pulsing, and far too much like skin. I take my hand back.
lines.I press my ear close. A wet, rhythmic gu: Ear to the pipe: a wet, steady gurgle. Something is being pumped through the ship.
lines.Metal grating covers green-glowing tubes: Metal grating over green-glowing tubes. Something below hums like a slow heartbeat.
lines.The grating is bolted down with organic: The rivets have grown into the floor. It won't budge.
lines.I whisper into the grate. My voice disap: I whisper into the grate. The dark below swallows it without an echo.
lines.A wall-mounted status panel showing the: A wall panel showing the containment deck's emergency state.
lines.The panel has gone from red to a frantic: The panel strobes orange now, the repeating symbol crossed out: containment breach. Somewhere a very organized alien is having a very bad day.
lines.A status panel pulses with dull red ligh: A status panel pulses red, one symbol repeating, probably about me. Red means danger in any language. The security hub to the right might let me into these systems.
lines.The panel still pulses red, but now I ca: Thanks to the security console's translation overlays: 'Containment Deck 7: Multiple Breach Events.' One entry repeats with a moving marker. Something is patrolling the deck.
lines.I tap the panel. It chirps in response a: It chirps and cycles screens of alien text. Without the security systems I can't read it, but the flashing sections show which parts of the deck are breached.
lines.A small black cat with glowing purple-am: A small black cat with glowing purple-amber eyes. Nothing like it belongs on an alien harvester.
lines.A black cat sits perfectly still, watchi: A black cat watches me with purple-amber eyes, its fur faintly shimmering like starlight. How did it get here?
lines.I whisper to the cat. It blinks slowly,: I whisper to the cat. It blinks slowly, twice, deciding whether I'm worth its time.
lines.I crouch and hold out a hand. The cat co: The cat pushes into my palm and leans on my shin, purring like a small engine. Then it trots off, tail up, and looks back once, as if to make sure I'll remember it.
lines.The cat is gone. Only the memory of its: The cat is gone. Cats are like that.
lines.I make a grab for the cat. Better people: I grab for the cat. Better men have tried. It's gone before my hand arrives.
lines.Behind me, the corridor opens back into: Behind me, the corridor opens back into the stasis hold. Amber pod-light spills out.
lines.I head back through the corridor into th: I head back into the stasis hold.
lines.I trace my fingers along the archway. Th: The archway is warm and damp, like the inside of a throat.
lines.The stasis hold behind me hums with the: A hundred occupied pods hum back there. I'd rather not go back, but I might have to.
lines.A heavy armored door on the left wall. T: A heavy armored door on the left wall. Through its viewport: examination tables and specimen jars.
lines.The heavy door grinds open. The stench o: The heavy door grinds open. The chemical stink hits me at once.
lines.Something's changed. Fresh drag marks sc: Something's changed. Fresh drag marks score the lab floor toward the examination tables. Something was processed while I was gone.
lines.I push against the membrane-like door. I: The membrane door yields with a wet suck.
lines.A faint chemical smell wafts from the la: An acid, organic smell from the lab. Specimens being processed.
lines.The corridor stretches into darkness ahe: The corridor runs on into darkness. A purple glow pulses at the far end.
I walk on down the corridor into the purple glow of the feeding station.
lines.The feeding station is quieter. The ener: The feeding station is quieter. The barriers are dark and the middle cage stands open. The Keth-Vari is gone.
lines.The passage deeper into the ship feels w: Warmer that way. The walls are slick with condensation, I hope.
lines.From deeper in the corridor I hear a dis: A distant mechanical churning, like machinery built to keep something alive.
lines.The translucent panels part with a wet h: The panels part with a wet hiss. Monitors light a small control room.
lines.I feel along the right-side passage entr: Faint grooves beside the door. Alien signage, maybe, worn smooth.
lines.A low electronic hum emanates from the r: An electronic hum from the right. Screens are still running in there.
A heavy metal grate bolted to the floor. Warm air pulses up through the slats.
lines.A heavy ventilation grate is bolted into: A floor grate breathing warm air. Its bolts have the same bio-locks as every door on this deck. I'd need to override the containment locks to open it.
lines.The ventilation grate's bio-locks have r: The grate's bio-locks have released. It can be lifted now. Warm air and red emergency light rise from the shaft.
lines.The grate won't budge. Bio-organic bolts: It won't budge. The bio-bolts are part of the lockdown. I'd need to override the security system first.
lines.I heave the unlocked grate aside and squ: I heave the grate aside and squeeze down into the shaft. Below, everything is red.
lines.I grip the grate and pull. The bio-locks: The bio-locks hold firm. Whatever seals the doors keeps this shut too.
lines.The released grate lifts with a groan of: The released grate lifts with a groan. The shaft drops away into red emergency light.
lines.Air moves through the grate in rhythmic: Air moves through the grate in slow gusts. In, out. The ship breathes through these vents.
lines.The grate has slid off its seat. Below,: The grate is off. The shaft below glows red and the air is moving. Everything on this deck is coming for me. Down it is.
lines.My voice falls into the shaft and comes: Nothing answers from the shaft. Plenty is answering up here.
lines.Walls of drawers containing failed speci: Walls of drawers holding failed specimens. Most are sealed. One is partly open.
lines.I pull open an empty drawer and squeeze: I squeeze into an empty drawer and pull it shut. Click. Click. Click. The footsteps come in, stop, and go. I wait a long time before climbing out.
lines.Rows of drawers, floor to ceiling, each: Drawers floor to ceiling, each big enough for a body. The open one holds a membrane-wrapped shape about my size. It didn't survive collection.
lines.I slide the open drawer further out. The: Inside, a creature built much like me. Different species, close enough to be unsettling. It didn't make it. I nearly didn't either.
lines.\"How many of us have they processed?\": "How many have they processed?" The drawers just go on and on.
lines.A central examination surface with drain: A central examination slab with drainage channels and overhead lights.
lines.A slab designed for dissection. Drainage: A dissection slab, draining to the recycling vats, its lights aimed at a torso that isn't there. Freshly cleaned. Whoever runs this place is tidy.
lines.The slab's surface is slick with a thin: A thin film coats the slab. I wipe my fingers on my suit and think about something else.
lines.\"I don't want to think about what happe: "I don't want to know what happened here." The drainage grooves tell me anyway.
lines.The slab is cabled to the floor. I'm not: The slab is cabled to the floor. I'm not getting any closer than I have to.
lines.Large vats where failed specimens are di: Large vats where failed specimens are dissolved and reclaimed.
lines.Three vats of viscous green liquid, bubb: Three vats of bubbling green. Failed specimens become hull, gardens and instruments. Nothing is wasted, and nobody leaves.
lines.I reach toward the vat's rim but pull ba: The heat off the rim warns me away. I listen to it.
lines.The vats gurgle softly, almost digestive: The vats gurgle, almost like a stomach. They really don't waste anything.
lines.A neural connection tendril, severed dur: A severed length of neural tendril, torn loose when this section was damaged.
lines.A length of neural tendril, torn loose d: A torn length of neural tendril. The cut end still pulses with bio-electricity. It's gross. It might also be useful.
lines.I pick up the tendril and try not to shu: Warm and damp, like a severed worm, and it makes my fingers tingle. Plugged into the right port, it might get me into something keyed to their biology.
lines.\"A piece of the ship's nervous system,\: "A bit of the ship's nervous system." It twitches, as if it heard me.
lines.The sample is pinned to the examination: It's pinned down with thin metal spines and squirms weakly against them.
lines.A wall-mounted cabinet with bio-organic: A wall cabinet with bio-organic seals and alien hazard symbols.
lines.A wall-mounted cabinet sealed with bio-o: A cabinet sealed with bio-locks. The triangle-and-circle hazard marks read the same in Choir notation. Whatever's inside bites.
The seals are made for broad Choir appendages, not fingers. I'd need something sharp and thin to pry them open.
lines.The cabinet is open. Rows of bio-capsule: The cabinet is open. Color-coded racks of bio-capsules, and I don't know Choir chemistry well enough to touch any of them.
lines.A wide channel in the floor collecting r: A wide floor channel catching runoff from the vats and the slab.
lines.A wide drainage channel runs the length: A green channel of runoff flows back into the ship's recycling. Small things glint in the murk. I decide they're pebbles.
lines.I reach into the channel. The fluid is w: Warm, thick, and the hard thing I find is a bit of bone. I drop it back. Nothing useful here.
lines.The fluid gurgles softly as it drains. T: The channel gurgles as it drains. It sounds uncomfortably like digestion.
lines.My blood runs cold. Lying in the drawer: A human, like me, not long dead. His eyes are open; neat surgical marks cross his chest. I wasn't the first specimen to wake up.
lines.The dead man lies still in his drawer. T: The dead man lies still. The marks on his chest are neat and unhurried, which is the worst part. It won't happen to me.
A human, like me. I close his eyes. Cold but not stiff: not dead long. I wasn't the first to wake up, and the first didn't make it.
lines.His left hand is curled shut. Gently, I: His left hand is curled shut. I open it gently: a plain gold ring. I take it. Someone should carry it home.
lines.I've already closed his eyes. The only t: I've closed his eyes. All that's left to do for him is get out and tell someone.
lines.\"I'll tell someone you were here,\" I p: "I'll tell someone you were here." It's the one promise on this ship I can keep.
lines.A heavy carcass hook, sunk into the lip: A heavy carcass hook sunk in a drawer lip, for dragging bodies out. The tip is barbed. Barbed things catch, and they hold.
lines.I work the hook free of the drawer with: I work the hook free with a wet creak. Heavy, curved like a talon, with a thick eyelet at the top. I could tie a line to that.
lines.I eye the hook and the drawer it's burie: I eye the hook and its drawer. "Not me," I mutter. "Not today."
lines.The passage leads back to the feeding st: Back to the feeding station. I can hear the energy barriers humming.
lines.I retrace my steps back to the feeding s: I head back to the feeding station.
lines.I push against the passage opening. The: The membrane gives under my hand, then draws back to let me through.
lines.A faint mechanical hum drifts from the p: A mechanical hum from the next chamber. Something's running in there.
lines.An automated dispenser that drips grey n: A dispenser that drips grey nutrient paste into the troughs on a timer.
lines.A mechanical arm squirts grey slurry int: An arm squirts grey slurry into the troughs on a timer. It smells like wet cardboard and pennies. Sustenance, barely.
lines.I collect a tube of grey slurry from the: I fill a tube with grey paste. Wet cardboard and pennies. On a ship this hungry, food is currency.
lines.I read the dispenser's output gauge alou: Pale green fluid still cycles through the tubes. Something here is still being fed.
lines.Long troughs filled with grey nutrient p: Long troughs of grey nutrient paste for living specimens.
lines.Shallow troughs of grey nutrient paste,: Half-eaten paste, topped up automatically. Fresh scoop marks: something fed here recently.
lines.I dip a finger into the residue lining t: Thick, lukewarm, faintly coppery. I wipe my finger on my suit.
lines.\"What were they feeding in here?\" I wh: "What did they feed in here?" Something bigger than me, and the scrape marks say it didn't come willingly.
lines.The barriers are down. The middle enclos: The barriers are down and the middle enclosure stands empty. The override opened these too, and the Keth-Vari didn't wait around.
lines.Behind flickering energy barriers, livin: Behind flickering barriers pace a dog-like thing with too many legs and something mostly tentacles. They watch me like another prisoner, which I am.
lines.I try making sounds at the nearest creat: I make a sound at the nearest creature. It answers with a low, mournful one. No shared language, but a shared situation.
lines.My hand gets within inches before the ha: Inches away, the hair on my arm stands up. Invisible barrier, very real static. I'll pass.
lines.The emitters are buried in the ceiling a: The emitters are buried in ceiling and floor. I'd have to move the room first.
lines.A creature pacing behind the middle ener: A creature pacing behind the middle energy barrier, watching me with clever, sad eyes.
lines.Behind the middle energy barrier, a crea: A lean, grey-blue, four-armed creature my height paces behind the middle barrier, dark eyes tracking me. The monitor reads 'sapient, cooperative.' Maybe we can talk.
lines.The Keth-Vari watches me through the bar: The Keth-Vari watches me, four arms gesturing slowly. Two prisoners, both a long way from home.
lines.I reach toward the barrier. Static crack: Static crackles as I reach out. The creature shakes its head urgently: no. It's seen what the barrier does.
lines.It taps its own chest, slowly and carefu: It taps its chest slowly, the way I'd introduce myself to a child: "Keth." Again: "Vari." Then it points at me and waits.
lines.The creature stops pacing and approaches: It tries clicks, whistles, a deep thrum. Then it touches two hands together and points at me, then itself: you and me, same.
lines.The creature waits, watching me with tho: It waits, watching me. It pointed at me, then itself. Same. What do I say?
lines.The creature's four arms spread wide, a: Its arms spread wide: yes, exactly. It points to the corridor exit and mimes running. It wants me to go, and do what it can't.
lines.The creature cocks its head, processing: It sweeps an arm at the ship, traces a path, left, forward, down, and mimes doors parting. The airlock. It knows the layout. It taps the barrier: it's trapped, I'm not.
lines.The creature shudders, all four arms wra: It holds up three fingers and mimes something huge moving through walls, then points at the ceiling veins and spreads its arms. The Choir aren't just on this ship. They are the ship.
lines.I just nod. The creature nods back, an e: I nod. It nods back, a human gesture it must have learned watching. It touches its chest, points at me: remember me.
lines.The Keth-Vari stops pacing and comes to: The Keth-Vari comes to the barrier, four hands resting against the static, waiting.
lines.It mimes crawling, then jerks its hands: It mimes crawling, snatches its hands back from an opening and blows on its palms: hot wind. It taps the scorched frame and shakes its head hard. Scorched mouths mean death. Then it draws a long winding line in the air: it knows the way, and wants out first.
lines.The creature goes very still. Then it pr: It goes still, then presses its forehead to the barrier with a long, low sound. It has heard promises before. It chooses to believe this one.
lines.I squeeze the nutrient paste through the: I push the paste through the gap at the barrier's base. It sniffs, then wolfs it down and lays all four hands on the barrier. We're allies now.
lines.Small screens above each energy barrier: Small screens above each enclosure showing specimen data.
lines.Vital signs, feeding schedules, behavior: Alien script, but numbers are numbers: some of these creatures have been here for decades. The middle one is noted 'communicative: further study warranted.'
lines.I tap one of the screens. It cycles thro: Weight, metabolism, aggression index. The middle occupant is flagged 'sapient, cooperative.' It might be able to help.
lines.A passage at the far end of the feeding: A passage at the far end. A faint chemical smell drifts out.
lines.I duck through the low passage. The air: I duck through the low passage. Colder air, stronger chemicals.
lines.I push through a heavy membrane that ser: The membrane door peels apart reluctantly, like wet tissue.
lines.A draft of cold, sterile air rolls out f: Cold, sterile air rolls out of the morgue. Chemicals, and something older under them.
lines.A dark passage on the far left leads bac: A dark passage on the far left leads back to the containment corridor. Its orange light bleeds through.
lines.I head back through the passage toward t: I head back toward the containment corridor.
lines.I duck under a low archway of fused bone: I duck under an arch of fused bone and chitin, back toward the main corridor.
lines.The corridor echoes back at me, a wet, r: The corridor echoes back, wet and hollow. I've had cosier conversations.
lines.A heavy door on the right wall. Through: A heavy door on the right wall. Through its viewport: rows of specimen containers and data crystals.
lines.I push through the heavy door into the c: I push through into the cold, dry air of the Specimen Archive.
lines.I slide open the archive door. It moves: The archive door slides smoothly, the only well-maintained thing I've seen aboard.
lines.Faint crystalline harmonics drift from t: Faint crystal harmonics drift from the archive, just at the edge of hearing.
lines.Frantic gouges in the floor of the open: Frantic gouges round and round the cage floor, four hands' worth. Whatever it scratched, it meant nothing to anyone but itself.
lines.I run my fingers over the gouges. Just m: Just marks. Whatever this was, it wasn't for me.
lines.Fresh gouges in the floor of the open ca: Fresh gouges in the cage floor: a long winding line through a grid of little squares, three squares crossed out hard. The ducts. The Keth-Vari kept its promise.
lines.The scratched route. I have it copied on: The scratched route. It's copied onto my map now.
lines.I trace the scratches with a fingertip a: I copy every turn onto my map, and cross out the three squares it crossed out. Now I know the way through the ducts.
lines.\"Thank you,\" I tell the empty cage. So: "Thank you," I tell the empty cage. Somewhere above, something four-armed is moving fast.
lines.Deep scratches gouged into the ventilati: Deep scratches gouged into the shaft walls. Someone escaped this way before.
lines.Deep gouges in the organic walls, made b: Gouges in the walls: arrows and a crude map of the ducts. A junction ahead splits left and right. The right way is marked with arrows; the left ends in a deep, angry X.
lines.You trace the scratch-map with your fing: I memorize the scratch-map, drawn north-up: from the junction an arrow runs EAST to a little lever, then all the way back WEST past here to a skull (bad air) and on, deeper. Little skulls mark ducts that breathe fire.
"Thanks," I tell whoever made these. They're too deep for fingernails, which raises questions.
lines.The scratches are gouged into the wall i: The scratches are cut into the wall itself. Whoever made them is long gone.
lines.The scattered remains of a small creatur: The scattered bones of a small creature that didn't make it through the shaft.
lines.Small bones scattered against the shaft: Small bones against the shaft wall: two legs, a skull, about my size. Another escapee. The claw marks nearby might be theirs.
lines.You examine the remains carefully. The b: Old, dry bones, with scraps of the same stuff my pod was made of. They broke out too. They just didn't get far.
lines.\"I'll make it,\" you tell the bones. Th: "I'll make it," I tell the bones. They're polite enough not to mention how many have said that.
lines.A sealed maintenance access panel in the: A sealed maintenance panel in the shaft wall.
lines.A maintenance access hatch set into the: A maintenance hatch, its organic rivets calcified shut. Through its little window: a tangle of pumping veins and nerve-like fibres.
lines.You pull at the hatch. The organic rivet: The rivets flex but hold; they've fused over time. I'd need something sharp to pry them loose.
lines.You tap on the hatch. A hollow echo come: I knock. A hollow echo: there's space behind it.
lines.The vent shaft opening leads back up to: The shaft opening leads back up to the containment corridor.
lines.The shaft opening behind you leads back: The opening behind me leads back up to the containment corridor.
lines.You haul yourself back up through the ve: I haul myself back up into the containment corridor.
lines.You brace yourself against the shaft wal: I brace against the walls and pull myself back toward the corridor.
lines.Your voice echoes up the shaft, bouncing: My voice bounces up the shaft toward the corridor.
lines.The ventilation shaft continues forward: The shaft continues forward into branching darkness.
lines.The shaft ahead splits into multiple dir: The shaft ahead splits several ways. Red emergency lights flicker in the distance.
lines.You crawl forward through the ventilatio: I crawl forward. The walls pulse faintly. Ahead, the tunnel opens into a junction.
lines.You feel the warm air flowing from ahead: Warm air flows from ahead. Onward, then.
lines.Your voice echoes down the shaft and com: My voice echoes down the shaft and comes back wrong.
lines.Scratch marks at the junction where the: Scratch marks where the vent splits.
Scratches at the junction. Without context, they're just gouges.
lines.Cross-referencing with your map: these a: These match the scratches in the cage. EAST first, to the lever. Then back WEST past here to the skull: bad air, so I'll want the helmet on.
The scratches are deep, made with desperate force.
lines.\"Which way...\" The tunnels swallow you: "Which way..." The tunnels swallow my whisper.
lines.Bio-organic pipes running along the ceil: Bio-organic pipes along the junction ceiling.
lines.Thick bio-organic pipes run along the ce: Ceiling pipes branch with the tunnel. The left ones hiss with chemical vapor; the right ones are dry and cracked.
lines.The pipes are warm and faintly sticky. Y: Warm and faintly sticky. I let go quickly.
lines.The pipes gurgle back. You decide that w: The pipes gurgle back. I decide that was a yes.
lines.You can feel different air currents from: Different air comes from each tunnel.
lines.The air behaves differently at the junct: From the LEFT, a sour chemical haze just hangs there: dead air. From the RIGHT, a faint, steady draught that has come a long way, so it's going somewhere.
lines.You hold your hand up to the currents. L: I hold up a hand. Left: still and sour. Right: a cool, steady pull.
lines.You sniff the air. The left tunnel smell: The left tunnel smells like a cupboard nobody opens. The right smells like a way out.
lines.The left tunnel. A faint yellowish haze: The left tunnel. A yellowish haze curls out, sharp and chemical.
lines.West, on your map. The ducts beyond bran: West, on the map: the long way, for after the lever.
lines.You crawl into the left tunnel. It opens: I crawl into the left tunnel: more ducts, ribbed, red and all alike. Ahead, the air has a chemical tang.
lines.The walls of the left tunnel are slick w: The left tunnel's walls are slick with chemical condensation.
lines.Your voice sounds muffled in the thicken: My voice comes out muffled in the thick air of the left tunnel.
lines.The right tunnel is darker. The air from: The right tunnel is darker and narrower, but a faint, steady draught comes out of it.
lines.East, on your map. More ducts, more bran: East, on my map. More ducts, more branches.
lines.You squeeze into the right tunnel. It br: I squeeze into the right tunnel. It branches almost at once into ducts that all look the same.
lines.The walls of the right tunnel are dry an: The right tunnel's walls are dry and cracked. No chemical damp here.
lines.Your voice falls flat in the dead air of: My voice runs away down the right tunnel on the draught.
lines.The tunnel leads back to the ventilation: The tunnel leads back to where I climbed in.
I crawl back to the shaft entry. The corridor's glow above is oddly reassuring.
lines.You brace against the walls as you back: I brace against the walls and back up.
lines.A Choir quarantine seal, a door of rivet: A Choir quarantine seal, riveted bronze. Through a crack, something pale and wet stretches across the opening, breathing.
lines.The seal stands open. Across the opening: The seal stands open. Beyond it the colony has grown a taut, wet membrane across the opening to keep the gas out.
lines.The seal won't move. A Choir lock: the r: The seal won't budge. A Choir lock: the release must be somewhere else in the ducts, probably far from here.
lines.You push into the membrane. It clings, s: The membrane clings, stretches, peels my helmet off like fruit skin and spits me out on a ledge. Above, a sky of breathing ribs. Below, a city.
lines.Your whisper runs away down the duct and: My whisper runs off down the duct and comes back as a dozen.
The duct behind me is sealed.
lines.Behind you the duct is sealed with a rid: A ridged lip seals the duct behind me. No way back.
lines.The duct runs on ahead, wet and breathin: The duct runs on. Its mouth is a ring of muscle: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath blows me back. Go when it opens.
lines.The duct breathes out as you go, and the: It breathes out as I go, and the gust shoves me back where I started.
lines.The duct breathes in and pulls you throu: The duct breathes in and pulls me through. Air! (+3)
lines.A soft opening in the right wall, rimmed: A soft, veined opening on the right. A ring of muscle: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath blows me back. Go when it opens.
lines.The way you came. The walls close in a l: The way I came. The walls squeeze in behind me, then relax.
lines.The duct runs on ahead, soot-black, its: The duct runs on, soot-black, its seams glowing orange.
Hot. I snatch my hand back.
lines.A side duct in the right wall, hot to lo: A side duct in the right wall, too hot to like.
lines.A thin grate onto a Choir hall, its ligh: A thin grate onto a Choir hall, light falling through in stripes.
lines.Through the grate: a Choir hall, too tal: Through the grate, a vast Choir hall lit cold blue. Something very large could reach in here. Only here.
lines.You touch the grate and pull your hand b: I touch the grate and pull back. On the other side, something heard that.
lines.You tap the call-stone on the grate. For: I tap the call-stone on the grate. Far off, the colony knocks back, hundreds of soft knocks. The hum behind the grate turns and goes the wrong way.
lines.You tap the stone on the grate. Nothing: I tap the stone on the grate. Nothing answers: it's spent until I start the Core again.
lines.Scalding air gusts out of this duct in s: Scalding air gusts out in slow pulses; the mouth is scorched black. Something vents hard through here.
lines.You crawl into the scorched duct. Halfwa: I crawl into the scorched duct. Halfway in, the metal starts to tick and shudder.
lines.The duct breathes out. Unfortunately, yo: The duct breathed out. You were in it. Purge ducts are scorched, glow with heat and have small skulls on the map: LOOK before you crawl.
lines.The membrane is clenched shut, hard as a: The membrane is clenched shut like a fist. It'll relax once the surge has passed.
lines.You press yourself into the cold fold. T: I press into the cold fold. The flesh closes over me and I keep very still.
lines.You put your face to the fold and breath: I put my face to the fold and breathe the cold hull air. My head clears.
lines.A crease in the wall where the hull's co: A frosted crease where hull cold seeps in. Air, and a hiding place: HAND it to press in.
lines.Your breath fogs in the cold air. Somewh: My breath fogs. Somewhere behind the fold, the hull ticks.
lines.A side duct in the left wall, hot to loo: A side duct in the left wall, too hot to like.
lines.Something pale and many-legged crouches: Something pale and many-legged at the edge of the haze, eyeless head raised, slits fluttering. It won't enter the gas. I blink: gone.
lines.It flinches back before you're anywhere: It flinches back before I'm anywhere near, and is gone down the duct.
lines.Its breathing slits flutter at you: long: Its breathing slits flutter at me: long, short, long. Then it flees.
lines.The duct runs on ahead, soot-black, its: Soot-black, seams glowing. Its mouth is a ring of muscle: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath vents scalding air. Go when it opens.
The vent fires as I go.
lines.Purge vents fire fast and out of step. L: Purge vents fire fast and out of step. Go on the in-breath, when the throat gulps, never the out-breath. Watch one cycle first; the cat, if it's with you, always goes on the in-breath.
lines.The vent gulps and pulls you through on: The vent gulps and pulls me through on hot air. (+3)
lines.A side duct in the left wall, hot to loo: A hot side duct on the left. Its throat: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath vents scalding air. Go when it opens.
lines.The black cat from upstairs, sitting by: The black cat from upstairs, sitting by the vent like it owns it. As the throat opens, it strolls through. Of course.
lines.It allows one scratch behind the ears, t: It allows one scratch behind the ears, then stares at the vent. On the in-breath, it's saying. Go when it opens.
lines.A soft opening in the left wall, rimmed: A soft, veined opening on the left. A ring of muscle: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath blows me back. Go when it opens.
lines.A side duct in the right wall, hot to lo: A hot side duct on the right. Its throat: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath vents scalding air. Go when it opens.
lines.A tight knot of membrane, grown over a h: A tight knot of membrane grown over a hole in the wall. The colony keeps it shut.
lines.The knot of membrane has relaxed into an: The knot has relaxed into an open ring: a tunnel the colony opened for me.
lines.The knot of membrane doesn't open for yo: The knot of membrane doesn't open for me.
I squeeze through the colony's tunnel.
lines.In the right-hand wall, a ring of cartil: In the right wall, three closed leaflets of muscle in a ring of cartilage: a heart valve, big enough to crawl through if it opened.
lines.In the left-hand wall, the back of the H: In the left wall, the back of the Heart Valve.
lines.A worker lies curled on its side, skin g: A worker lies curled, blotched grey where the gas got it, slits opening in a wet, broken rhythm.
lines.You lay a hand on its side. It flinches,: I lay a hand on its side. It flinches, then goes still. Nothing left to fight with.
lines.A nest of shed skins and egg crust, and: Thumb-sized pale grubs wriggle in a nest of shed skins and egg crust. Their mouths are mostly teeth. Best not to reach in.
lines.The grubs scatter from your hand like yo: The grubs scatter from my hand like I'm one of them. The colony knows me now.
lines.You reach into the nest. Every grub turn: I reach into the nest. Every grub turns toward my hand at once.
lines.Larvae nests sit in dead ends: skins, eg: Larvae nests sit in dead ends. LOOK first and leave them be. (Once the Queen accepts you, they scatter instead.)
lines.The heap goes quiet, listening. Then wri: The heap goes quiet, listening. Then it wriggles again.
lines.The duct ends a few yards in; you can se: The duct ends a few yards in. From the back wall, a voice: "Outrider, respond. Outrider, respond." Same words, same breath, every time.
lines.\"Outrider, respond. Outrider...\" The v: "Outrider, respond. Outrider..." So close now. The duct ends, and something unfolds out of the dark where the voice was.
lines.The voice repeated itself exactly, every: The voice never changed, and LOOK said the duct ends. Mission Control is far away. Once the Queen accepts you, her guard deals with this thing.
lines.The dead end is empty now: a long, torn: A torn shed skin, and a Warden over it. The Queen's guard dealt with the Mimic. The Warden lowers its head to me.
lines.\"Outrider, respond,\" you say, just to: "Outrider, respond," I say, just to hear it. The Warden's slits flare. Nobody answers.
lines.The duct you came out of. The membrane h: The duct I came out of. The membrane has closed over it, gas behind. No going back.
lines.The membrane has sealed behind you. Ther: The membrane has sealed behind me. No going back through the gas now.
lines.The pale scout from the Outer Ducts, wai: The pale scout from the Outer Ducts. It watched me cross the gas it couldn't, and now scuttles into the city to tell someone.
lines.On a far rib above the city, a small bla: On a far rib, the cat from upstairs licks a paw. The Vesk find its breathing strange and leave it be.
lines.The Keth-Vari, perched on a rib among th: The Keth-Vari, perched among the honeycomb homes. "Wall-mothers," it says, with a breathy sound that might be a laugh.
lines.\"You came down after all.\" Four hands: "You came down after all." Four hands scratch the torn half onto my map: folds, ducts, a curl for the court. "She wants three things. Speak her way. Give up the Choir's mark. A promise." It taps my tag. "That, first."
It clasps my hand in two of its four. "Go on. They're watching you."
lines.Workers, each the size of a cat, carry f: Cat-sized workers carry food and egg crust along the ledge, breathing at each other in passing. A whole city of them.
lines.They freeze at your voice, slits wide, t: They freeze at my voice, slits wide, then hurry on.
lines.A woman, or what the colony kept of one:: A woman the colony grew into the wall, Vesk slits breathing round her face. Her old flight suit reads HALLORAN.
lines.\"Thirty years,\" she says. Her voice is: "Thirty years," she says thinly; her lungs clean the colony's air. "The Choir threw me down here to die. The Vesk grew me into the wall to live. They chose kindness."
lines.\"In breath. Long, short, long: that's t: "Long, short, long: their greeting. It means I come to listen. Breathe it at the royal guard and it'll let you pass." She shows me: a long exhale, a short, a long.
lines.\"By moving air. They sweep the same loo: "By moving air. They sweep the same loops on a rhythm, clicking a few seconds before they come. Get in a cold fold and hold still. In the Warren, move with the wind."
lines.\"To stop being burned. The Choir fire t: "To stop the burning. The Choir fire the Purge Core, scald the border ducts and gassed the door. The young die first. They need someone small who can turn a Choir valve. You."
lines.\"Two things I could ask. Take my name h: "I could ask two things. Take my name home. Or..." She looks at the slits breathing for her. "Let me stop."
lines.She works the patch loose from her suit: With stiff fingers she works the patch off her suit and gives it to me. "Halloran. Life support. Tell them I kept the air clean to the end."
lines.You hold her hand while the slits around: I hold her hand while her slits slow, and stop. Below, the Warren's lights dim and the colony breathes out.
lines.Through a crack in the hull, cold air, s: Through a crack in the hull: cold air, stars, and the blue edge of Earth. Closer than I thought.
lines.Cold enough to burn. You breathe it in,: Cold enough to burn. I breathe it in. Best air I've had in my life.
lines.Through the grate, far below: the Curato: Far below, the Curator plots the next purge on a map of the Core, the Purge Heart marked far north-west. It hums as it works, a low wandering note. I'll know that hum again.
lines.\"The Penitent still sings,\" you whispe: "The Penitent still sings," I whisper. Far below, the Curator goes still, then works on, slower.
lines.Candles of rendered fat in the rib-niche: Fat candles burn in the rib-niches. Scratched into the bone, over and over, one word in Choir glyphs. I can't read it. It looks like an apology.
lines.A Choir face, grey and gaunt, grafted in: A gaunt grey Choir face, grafted among bones and candles. Its eyes open, as big as the Curator's. It is weeping.
lines.\"Small one.\" Its voice is a chord with: "Small one." A cracked chord of a voice. "I refused to fire a purge, so they grafted me here to hear every one. The Vesk keep me alive. I am the only Choir that ever spared them."
lines.\"The Purge Core is a furnace. Every few: "The Core is a furnace. Every few minutes a hot wind rolls along the north ducts: hide in a fold when it roars. The Purge Heart drives it, the fan at the Core's far end, and it blows the gas. Jam it, and both stop."
lines.\"Something long and strong in its drive: "Something long and strong in its drive, where muscle meets axle. Your probe, or the Choir multitool the Collector keeps in the Cache, in the Core's east. Be quick: the Curator will guess."
lines.\"The Heart Valve, near the middle of th: "The Heart Valve, mid-Gut. It opens for stasis fluid. Or a song." It hums a long, low chord. "Go to the valve. I will sing it open for you."
lines.Its skin is cold and smooth. The eyes cl: Cold, smooth skin. The eyes close, as if the touch is more than it can bear.
lines.Egg sacs, hundreds, glowing amber in the: Hundreds of egg sacs glow amber in the walls. The ones by the north wall are blackened. Burned.
lines.Warm. Something inside turns toward your: Warm. Something inside turns toward my hand.
The way north, deeper, to the Queen.
lines.You go down into the Queen's chamber. Yo: I go down into the Queen's chamber, feeling very small.
lines.A Warden twice the size of any you've se: A Warden twice the size of the rest, coiled round a basket of young. Nobody passes without the colony's greeting.
lines.The guard's head lowers toward you, slit: The guard lowers its head toward me, slits wide. Waiting for something.
lines.Long. Short. Long. I come to listen. The: Long. Short. Long. I come to listen. The guard lowers its head to the floor and uncoils from the way north.
lines.Your voice means nothing to it. It hisse: My voice means nothing to it. It hisses. I need their greeting; someone in the Gut must know it.
lines.You back away slowly. It watches you all: I back away slowly. It watches me all the way.
It lowers its head as I pass.
lines.You reach toward it. It rises, and keeps: I reach toward it. It rises, and keeps rising. I put my hand down.
lines.A wide hole in the floor of the brood ch: A hole ringed with chewed flesh, opened for me: a way down into the Purge Core, about halfway through.
lines.A wide hole in the floor, ringed with ch: A wide hole ringed with chewed flesh, guarded by the young. Not for strangers.
lines.You climb down to the lip of the drop-ho: I climb down to the lip of the drop-hole.
lines.The wall behind the Queen: living muscle: Behind the Queen, clenched muscle and heat beyond: the border into the Purge Core.
lines.The border stands open, a ring of relaxe: The border stands open, a ring of relaxed muscle. Heat breathes through from the Core.
lines.At the border the Keth-Vari catches up w: At the border the Keth-Vari catches up, bends a claw into a ring and presses it onto my finger. "I stay with the wall-mothers. We'll fight from in here. Go."
lines.The Queen's guard walks you to the borde: The Queen's guard walks me to the border. No Vesk goes further. The heat hits like a hand. Now it's me, my breath, and her gifts.
lines.Warm muscle, and on the far side of it,: Warm muscle, and heat on the far side.
lines.The Queen. She fills the chamber: vast a: The Queen fills the chamber, vast and pale, amber slits glowing, brood crawling over her. For three hundred cycles she has watched the Choir burn her children.
lines.She smells the Choir on you: the tag the: She smells the Choir on me: the tag, still counting down. "What are you to them?" breathes through the chamber.
lines.The brood swarm up your arm, a hundred t: The brood swarm up my arm and eat the signal out of the tag. The countdown stops; the Choir have lost my trail. She knows that mark well.
lines.The brood swarm up your arm and strip th: The brood strip the last Choir scent from where the tag was clipped. The chamber stops smelling of Choir.
lines.She knows a lie by your breath. The broo: She knows a lie by my breath. The brood hiss. She asks again.
lines.You go for her. She is a queen in her ow: I go for her. She is a queen in her own court.
lines.Attacking the Queen in her own court, su: Attacking the Queen in her own court was the Audience's one fatal answer. Every other wrong turn only sends you back a step.
lines.You swear it. The whole chamber breathes: I swear it. She gives me a lung-sac to carry air, a call-stone to make her people knock on the walls, and an egg "for wherever you go". Behind her, the border into the Purge Core unclenches.
lines.\"A trade, then.\" She gives you a lung-: "A trade, then." A lung-sac, nothing else. Behind her, the border into the Purge Core unclenches.
lines.You won't promise. The guard escorts you: I won't promise. The guard escorts me back to the egg sacs. "Come back when you are ready," breathes after me. "I will wait."
lines.Her side is warm and vast, rising and fa: Her side is warm and vast. She breathes, and lifts me off my feet and sets me down.
lines.She smells it and lets it go. She wants: She smells it and lets it go. She wants me, not my things.
lines.A torn scrap of map pinned to the wall b: A torn scrap of map: the torn half of the Gut, in a careful human hand. Folds circled, a curl in the north for the court.
lines.You copy her scrap onto your map, line f: I copy her scrap onto my map, line for line. The torn half isn't blank any more.
lines.A rolled thermal blanket, a book with it: A thermal blanket, a coverless book, a lantern burning fat. Someone lived here a long time.
lines.A woman in a burned orange flight suit,: A woman in a burned orange flight suit, curled toward the wall, scorched down one side the way the Core burns. She tried it alone, came back, and lay down.
lines.You close her eyes. Her specimen tag is: I close her eyes. Her specimen tag is still on her wrist, counting down nothing.
lines.Her journal. \"Their greeting: long, sho: Her journal: "Their greeting: long, short, long. I come to listen. The Queen turned me away; the Choir's mark was still on me, and I couldn't give it up. I'll try the Core alone." The rest is blank.
lines.You read it through. The greeting: long,: I read it through. The greeting: long, short, long. And the Queen turned her away because of the tag.
lines.The walls are grown all over with small,: Thousands of small soft ears cover the walls, every one turned toward the dark at the end of the hollow.
lines.A vast old grub, pale and blind, half-su: A vast blind grub half-sunk in a pool, ringed by ears. The colony's memory: it keeps everything it has heard.
lines.The Archivist turns its blind head towar: The Archivist turns its blind head to me. Its whole body is a throat. What do I ask it to play?
lines.Rain. A warm wet world breathing. Then a: Rain on a warm wet world. Then the sky tearing, siphon beams, soil and larvae riding up into the dark. The Choir ate their world; the Vesk survived inside it.
It breathes for me: long, short, long. "I come to listen." Again, slower, until I have it.
lines.A woman's voice, hoarse: \"She won't tak: A hoarse woman's voice: "She won't take me while the Choir's mark is on me. It's the last thing that says where I came from." Crying, then footsteps going away down a duct.
lines.A burst of static, then, crisp and impos: Static, then, crisp and impossible: "Outrider, this is Mission Control, do you read?" Stolen from something that steals voices. Worth remembering.
lines.Soft, warm, and the whole body hums unde: Soft and warm; the whole body hums under my palm like a held note.
lines.On the pedestal, a Choir maintenance too: A Choir tool: a long bone-handled rod with folding prongs. Long and strong. It would jam a fan.
I lift the multitool. Heavy and warm, made for hands three times mine.
lines.Shelves of trophies from worlds the Choi: Trophies of eaten worlds: masks, shells, a skull with too many eye sockets. On the right, a Vesk carving of a Vesk, from a world that's gone.
lines.A heavy maintenance lever on a riveted b: A heavy lever on a bronze plate, warning light dull red. Beside it, in Choir glyphs and scratched human letters: "GAS DOOR - WEST".
lines.The lever is down and its light glows am: The lever is down, its light amber. Far to the west, the Gas Chamber's quarantine seal is open.
I hang my weight on the lever. It grinds down, the light turns amber, and far to the west something heavy unlocks with a boom.
lines.The Heart Valve: three leaflets of pink: The Heart Valve: three pink muscle leaflets clenched in cartilage. The Penitent said stasis fluid, or a song.
lines.You pour the stasis fluid over the leafl: I pour the stasis fluid over the leaflets. They shiver, slacken and fold open, and stay that way.
lines.You hum at it. It doesn't care for your: I hum at it. It doesn't care for my singing.
I crawl through the open valve.
lines.You look down. A long way down, heat and: A long way down to heat and orange seams. Too far to drop. The bone knuckle on the right wall would hold a line.
lines.You tie the line to the bone knuckle and: I tie the line to the bone knuckle and climb down into the heat, dropping the last few feet. The line stays, swinging.
lines.You lower yourself over the edge and let: I lower myself over the edge and let go.
lines.The drop-hole is a long fall into the Pu: The drop-hole is a long fall. LOOK down first: the bone knuckle on the wall would hold your grappling line.
lines.A thick bio-organic pipe has split open: A fleshy pipe split open like a wound, pouring yellow-green vapor in pulses. The dissolved remains nearby say how toxic it is.
lines.You reach toward the pipe and immediatel: I reach for the pipe and jerk back: the gas burns on contact. I need protection before touching anything in here.
lines.With the helmet protecting you, you exam: Behind the helmet I can look close. The ship's flesh has torn open here, and there's no way to seal it.
lines.The gas hisses from the pipe like a warn: The gas hisses from the pipe like a warning.
lines.A specimen larger than the one in the en: A big body, half-dissolved by the gas. A Choir uniform clings to the torso.
lines.You lean closer to examine the body. The: I lean closer. The gas burns my eyes, my throat, my lungs...
lines.With the helmet sealing out the gas, you: Helmet sealed, I look closer. Choir crew, fleeing their own ship, badge corroded past reading. No protection for this section.
lines.\"You almost made it,\" you whisper to t: "You almost made it," I whisper. The gas swirls around them.
lines.The tunnel continues through the gas tow: The tunnel goes on through the gas toward a distant mechanical sound.
lines.The tunnel continues forward through the: The tunnel goes on through the thickest gas, toward a distant grinding. I won't survive that without breathing protection.
lines.The tunnel continues through the gas. Wi: The tunnel goes on through the gas. With the helmet, I could make it. Beyond the haze, a rhythmic grinding.
lines.You push deeper into the gas. Your eyes: I push into the gas. My eyes stream. My throat closes. I can't breathe...
lines.You hold your breath, which works for ab: You held your breath, which works for about nine seconds. That helmet in Security would have looked very good on you.
lines.The helmet's visor seals as you push on: The visor seals and I push on through the gas, past the curled bodies, to the door at the far end.
lines.You feel the air current pushing against: Air pushes against me from deeper in. Something ahead is moving a lot of it.
lines.The grinding sound from ahead reverberat: Grinding echoes through the gas from up ahead.
lines.The duct back the way you came. The air: The duct back the way I came. Cleaner air that way.
lines.You retreat from the gas, back into the: I back out of the gas into the ducts. The air clears as I crawl.
lines.You brace against the walls, backing awa: I brace on the walls and back away from the haze.
lines.\"I need to find another way… or get pro: "Another way, or a helmet. Preferably a helmet."
lines.Three pale, many-legged things lie curle: Three pale many-legged bodies, curled where the gas caught them, bigger nearer the door. Trying to get out, or get something in.
lines.Through the glove the body is soft and c: Soft and cold through the glove. Whoever made this gas made it for them.
lines.Nothing answers. Something, a long way o: Nothing answers. Far off behind the walls, something breathes in.
lines.The Purge Heart: a fan as big as the duc: The Purge Heart: a duct-sized fan, five blades spinning, Choir gas canisters strapped to its hub. It drives the purges and blows the gas. Its drive is on the right wall, where muscle meets axle.
lines.The fan blades are locked in place, froz: The blades are frozen, my bent probe wedged in the drive. Room to squeeze between them.
lines.You'd lose your arm. The blades are movi: I'd lose the arm. Those blades are moving far too fast.
Cold, still blades. They won't move while the probe holds. I could squeeze between them.
lines.You push against the wind toward the spi: I push against the wind toward the blades. One catches me...
lines.You walked into a giant spinning fan. Th: You walked into a giant spinning fan. The ventilation works perfectly, though. Next time, jam it first.
lines.You carefully squeeze between the jammed: I turn sideways and squeeze between the jammed blades. Fresher air on the other side. I'm through.
lines.The fan drowns out your voice with its r: WHUMP. WHUMP. WHUMP. The fan wins the conversation.
lines.In the silence of the stopped fan, you c: With the fan stopped, I can hear my own breathing.
lines.You drive the Choir multitool into the d: I jam the multitool into the drive and open its prongs. The Heart chokes and stops, the seams go dark, the gas thins. Far behind me, the ducts fill with breathing: the colony, crossing the border.
lines.The fan's drive mechanism is exposed — b: Muscle round a metal axle, straining. A gap in the housing would take something long, thin and strong to jam it.
lines.Your surgical probe is wedged firmly in: My probe is wedged in the gears. The muscle strains against it, but it holds. The probe's done for anything else.
lines.The mechanism is too powerful to stop by: Those muscles would tear my arm off. I need a tool to wedge into the gap in the housing.
lines.The probe is locked in place. You couldn: The probe is locked in place. It isn't coming out.
lines.You ram the probe into the drive where t: I ram the probe in where muscle meets axle. The Heart chokes and stops, the seams go dark, the gas thins. Far behind me, the ducts fill with breathing: the colony, crossing the border for the first time.
lines.That won't fit in the mechanism gap. You: That won't fit the gap. I need something long, thin and sturdy enough to jam it.
lines.The mechanism pulses with a biological r: The muscle drives the fan like a heart drives blood.
The duct back the way I came.
lines.The ceiling has collapsed completely, se: The ceiling came down long ago; the ship grew over the rubble like scar tissue. No getting through.
lines.You push against the rubble. It doesn't: I push. The growth has fused it all into one solid mass. Sealed for good.
I shove the rubble. One pebble moves. The rest stays collapsed.
lines.Your voice bounces off the rubble wall a: My voice comes back flat off the rubble. Nothing beyond.
lines.A skeletal figure sits propped against t: A skeleton too big for a human, propped on the rubble: Choir crew, fleeing their own ship. A datapad still glows faintly in its bony hands.
lines.Without the datapad's glow, you notice s: Without the datapad's glow, I spot a faint pulse under the collar: something crystalline in a chest pocket.
lines.You carefully extract the datapad from t: I ease the datapad from its grip. The screen flickers; still charged. A Choir crewman's last record.
lines.You reach into the skeleton's chest pock: From the chest pocket, a warm crystal chip: a Choir security badge, still active. It might open doors deeper in.
Nothing left. I've taken the datapad and the chip.
lines.The skeleton sits empty-handed and strip: Empty-handed now: a Choir engineer who died in these same vents. The chip might still be useful.
lines.\"You were trying to get out too,\" you: "You were trying to get out too," I whisper. "How many have tried?"
lines.More scratches on the walls. These look: More scratches, deeper and more frantic than at the entry. Someone realised they'd chosen wrong.
lines.These match the X gouged on your map. Wh: Claw marks around a crude X. Whoever made them found this dead end first and warned the next one through.
lines.Deep enough to feel the desperation. Cla: Deep gouges. Claws, not tools: an alien made these, not a human.
lines.You back out of the dead end and into th: I back out of the dead end into the ducts.
lines.You brace against the narrow walls as yo: I brace on the narrow walls and back out.
lines.\"Nothing more here. Time to try the oth: "Nothing more here. The other way, then."
lines.Through a crack in the vent wall, you se: Through a crack in the wall: stars, cool and blue after all that red. A very long way from home.
lines.You press your face to the crack. The hu: I press my face to the cold crack. Vacuum, stars, and scarred hull. Something hit this ship hard.
lines.\"Stars…\" Your voice catches. You'd alm: "Stars." My voice catches. I'd almost forgotten there was an outside.
lines.The ventilation shaft opens into a large: Through the hatch below: docking clamps, an airlock bay and, is that a shuttle? The way out, or near it.
lines.You lower yourself through the hatch and: I drop through the hatch into the airlock bay. After the vents, it feels enormous. I made it.
lines.The hatch rim is smooth — this was a mai: A smooth maintenance hatch, not an escape route. It'll do.
lines.\"Almost there. Just a drop into the bay: "Almost there. Just a drop to the bay."
lines.The tunnel leads back to the fan room. T: The tunnel back to the fan room. The jammed blades still let me through.
lines.You crawl back through the jammed fan bl: I crawl back through the jammed fan blades.
lines.You brace yourself to squeeze back throu: I brace myself to squeeze back through the fan blades.
lines.\"Why would I go back? The airlock is ri: "Why go back? The airlock is right here."
lines.The main control station for containment: The deck's main security station. Screens show surveillance feeds.
lines.I lean in to examine the security consol: I lean in for a closer look at the console...
lines.I lean over the console and get my hands: I lean over the console and get my hands on the controls...
lines.The console is cabled into the floor. Be: It's cabled into the floor, and it's the only thing on this ship that's helped me. It stays.
lines.I mutter the alien symbols on the displa: I mutter the symbols on the display. A few keep recurring. Status codes, maybe. Or countdowns.
lines.One of the surveillance screens is badly: One surveillance screen is badly cracked. Someone fought here.
lines.The screen is cracked in a starburst pat: A starburst crack, scorch marks, a chair knocked over. Someone fought the Choir here and lost, but not quietly.
lines.I trace the crack with my finger. The gl: I trace the crack. The glass is warm, lit from inside by something bioluminescent.
lines.Pry it out with what, my fingernails? I': Pry it out with my fingernails? I've seen what happened to the last fellow's fingernails.
lines.The fractured display flickers between t: The broken display flickers between a lower-deck schematic and what might be a manifest. Both too corrupted to read.
lines.A drawer unit grown into the wall beside: A drawer grown into the wall beside the console, jammed half-open.
A drawer grown into the wall, jammed half-open. Inside, bio-organic key cards pulse faintly: access cards for the containment deck.
lines.The cards left in the drawer are a highe: The cards left in the drawer are a higher clearance. Too high for me.
lines.I work my fingers into the jammed drawer: I work a key card out of the jammed drawer. It pulses like a heartbeat: circuitry in compressed cartilage. It should open standard containment doors.
lines.I already have a key card. The remaining: I already have a key card. The rest are too high a clearance for me.
lines.A faint label above the drawer slot: thr: A faint label over the slot: three glyphs and a clearance level. The lowest tier, if I'm reading it right.
lines.The drawer slides on organic rails but w: It slides on organic rails but won't come out. It's grown into the wall.
