lines.An overturned chair with a snapped leg,: An overturned chair with a snapped leg.
lines.I crouch behind the overturned chair, kn: I crouch behind the chair, knees to my chest. Footsteps slow at the door, then move on. I breathe again.
lines.The chair is overturned, one leg snapped: One leg snapped clean off, and deep scratches in the floor beneath. Someone was dragged out of here.
lines.I right the chair. Underneath, scratch m: I right the chair. Underneath: five parallel gouges in the floor. Claws, or fingers holding on.
lines.A wall-mounted cabinet with a cracked gl: A wall cabinet with a cracked glass front and alien safety symbols.
lines.A wall-mounted emergency equipment cabin: An emergency cabinet. The symbols show a helmet and a breathing mask. The latch is stuck, but the glass is already cracked. I could force it.
lines.The emergency cabinet hangs open, its cr: The cabinet hangs open. Everything left is Choir-sized. The helmet slot is empty.
lines.I smash through the cracked glass and wr: I smash the cracked glass and wrench it open. Most of it is Choir-sized, but the helmet has a universal seal. It sits on me like a fishbowl, but it locks and breathes. Good for toxic air.
Nothing useful left. It's all Choir-sized.
lines.The safety symbols on the cabinet are cl: Helmet, breathing mask, protective gear. Safety symbols are universal, apparently.
lines.It's bolted to the wall. Someone on this: It's bolted to the wall. Someone here takes health and safety very seriously. Just not mine.
lines.I push aside a curtain of dangling neura: I push aside a curtain of dangling neural fibres and step into the corridor.
lines.The corridor hums faintly beyond the doo: The corridor hums beyond the doorway.
lines.The black cat has followed me in and is: The black cat has followed me and taken the console like it owns the place. Maybe it does. Nothing here bothers it.
lines.It allows exactly one scratch behind the: It allows exactly one scratch behind the ear. Then, holding my gaze, it pushes a stylus off the console. On purpose.
lines.\"Who's a good alien-ship cat?\" It blin: "Who's a good alien-ship cat?" It blinks slowly. I've been judged and found adequate.
lines.Multiple screens showing surveillance fe: Screens showing surveillance feeds from across the containment deck.
The feeds cycle: the corridor, the feeding station's glowing cages, the dark lab. A hunter drone ticks along a far passage, the same sweep every minute. I could time my moves around it.
lines.The surveillance feeds show the Curator': The feeds show the drone's sweep: Stasis Hold, corridor, feeding station, archive, then gone. Once a minute.
lines.I tap the screens. They're organic displ: I tap the screens. Warm, slightly soft. The feeds flicker but don't change.
lines.\"Show me where it is,\" I whisper to th: "Show me where it is," I whisper. It's a security console, not a personal assistant.
lines.A readout showing the current status of: A readout of the containment deck's systems.
lines.The status screen glows alarm-red, rings: Red readouts around a sensor like an eye. Containment locks ENGAGED. Vent grates SEALED. And a deck map: the ventilation shaft runs from the corridor to the airlock bay, if I can get that grate open. Beside a red cross: EMERGENCY OVERRIDE — NOT ARMED.
lines.The status display shows all containment: All containment locks DISENGAGED. Red warnings pulse across the map. I've opened everything.
lines.The display is a projection surface. My: It's a projection. My hand passes through and scrambles the readouts.
lines.I read the alien symbols aloud, trying t: I read the symbols aloud. Choir sounds like grinding stones. Nothing answers.
lines.A red emergency button under a cracked c: A red button under a cracked cowl, marked with a cross: a containment override. Not broken, just unarmed. Something elsewhere on the ship's network has to wake it.
lines.I press it. It sinks in limply and sprin: I press it. It sinks limply and springs back. It has to be armed from some other system on this deck.
lines.A red emergency button that appeared aft: A red emergency button, lit since the processing terminal was opened.
lines.The red emergency override button is glo: The override is glowing now; opening the processing terminal armed it. Pressing it will release every containment lock on this deck, including the vent grate in the corridor floor.
lines.I press the emergency override button. I: I press it. A wet click, then heavy thunks across the deck: every door, grate and seal on this level opens. Whatever patrols here will notice. On the feed, the middle barrier in the feeding station goes out. Four arms. A blur. Gone.
lines.My palm hovers over the button. The mome: My hand hovers. Once this goes, every hunter on the deck comes running, and I won't get back up here for anything I forgot. I'm not ready. I should think about what's waiting in those ducts, and beyond them.
lines.The override button is dark now — all co: The button is dark. Every lock is already open.
lines.Floor-to-ceiling racks of glowing data c: Floor-to-ceiling racks of glowing data crystals, each one a species' complete record.
lines.Thousands of data crystals, each humming: Thousands of crystals, some ancient and faded, some bright and new. Each one an entire species, catalogued and filed.
lines.I pull a crystal at random and slot it i: I slot a random crystal into the reader. A six-legged, furry, clever-eyed species, a lush green world, and the red symbol: consumed. I put it back.
lines.\"A library of the dead,\" I whisper. Ea: "A library of the dead," I whisper.
lines.The rack is fused to the wall. Taking a: It's fused to the wall. Taking a whole library home is frowned on everywhere, apparently.
lines.A crystal that's slightly different from: A crystal unlike the others: personal records, not specimen data.
lines.This crystal is different: smaller, a di: Smaller than the rest, a different hue, misfiled among the specimens. Its pulse is more complex. Personal data: a Choir officer's private log, maybe.
lines.I pocket the crystal. It holds notation: I pocket it. Alien script and maths I can't read yet, but it looks like part of a translation key. Find more fragments and I might read Choir writing.
lines.\"Someone recorded this. Someone who was: "Someone was here before me." The crystal pulses faintly, as if eager to talk.
lines.The crystal is small enough to carry. I: It's small enough to carry, if I can get it out of its slot.
lines.A pedestal-mounted device for reading da: A pedestal reader for data crystals that projects them as holograms.
lines.A crystalline reading device on an ornat: A crystal reader on an ornate pedestal. Slot a crystal in and it projects the contents above. Efficient and deeply impersonal.
lines.I slot the personal log crystal into the: I slot in the personal log. Dense alien text fills the air, threaded with star maps and sketches. Buried in it, partial translation keys. I'd need more fragments to finish the cipher, but it's a start.
lines.I run my fingers over the device's surfa: It flickers alien text at my touch and goes dark. It needs a crystal.
lines.\"If I can find a crystal that fits, I m: "Find a crystal that fits and I might learn something." The empty slot seems to agree.
lines.It's plumbed into the wall by cables thi: It's plumbed in with cables thicker than my arm. It stays.
lines.I pour stasis fluid into the reader's in: I pour stasis fluid into the reader's reservoir. It whirs up brighter; the fluid powers it. Now it can decode deeper layers of any crystal I insert.
I slot in my specimen tag. My vitals appear, and a label: 'Sol-3 Primate, Batch 7, Priority: LOW.' Not even high priority. And a schedule: Batch 7 is next.
lines.Holographic projections of cataloged wor: Holograms of catalogued worlds drift above the archive, most marked in red.
lines.Dozens of planets drift overhead in mini: Planets drift overhead: lush worlds, ice worlds, gas giants with inhabited moons. Nearly all marked with the red consumption symbol. Not dozens. Thousands, going back billions of years.
lines.\"Some kind of catalog system,\" I say,: "Some kind of catalogue," I say. Glyphs scroll in answer to my voice. I can't read any of them.
lines.I try to grab a planet. My hand goes str: I try to grab a planet. My hand goes straight through. Six-year-old me is thrilled anyway.
lines.I hold the neural tendril up to the holo: I hold the neural tendril to the display. It twitches, and the star map races past dead worlds to a blue one I'd know anywhere. The harvest glyph, and a ring of marks: eleven still lit. Eleven cycles until Earth is empty. The tendril goes dark, spent.
lines.I flick the hologram. A thousand worlds: I flick the hologram. A thousand red-marked worlds spin past like a slot machine and click to a stop on a small blue one. I don't like that at all.
lines.The right wall holds crystals that are d: The right wall holds darker crystals, almost black.
lines.These crystals are darker than the ones: Almost black, with violet cores, and labelled differently. Personal logs, mission reports? Not specimen data, anyway.
lines.I try to pull one free, but these are lo: Unlike the left rack, these are locked in. The Choir wanted these kept safe.
lines.I drop flat behind the benches and press: I drop flat behind the benches, cheek to the cold floor. Don't breathe.
lines.Two seats, worn smooth by long use. The: Two seats worn smooth. The Choir sat here to admire the worlds they'd stripped. A chapel to their own appetite.
lines.I sit down. The bench adjusts slightly t: I sit. The bench shifts to fit me. Front-row seat to the end of worlds.
lines.The heavy door leads back to the feeding: The heavy door back to the feeding station.
lines.I push back through the door into the wa: I push back through into the warm, humid feeding station.
lines.I feel along the passage walls. They're: The passage walls are polished smooth by countless things passing through.
lines.I hear a low rhythmic pulsing from beyon: A low rhythmic pulsing comes from beyond the passage, like a heartbeat.
lines.A large viewport showing the planet belo: A great viewport onto the planet below, beautiful and unaware it's dying.
lines.That's home. I'd know those coastlines a: That's home: North America under thin cloud, dusk rolling over the east coast. And falling on it from orbit, thin as threads, energy siphons. The Convergence isn't coming to Earth. It's already started.
lines.The viewport glass is ice-cold to the to: The glass is ice-cold. My fingerprints fog and fade.
lines.\"Hang on,\" I tell the planet. It's a r: "Hang on," I tell the planet. Ridiculous thing to say to a planet. I mean it anyway.
lines.Heavy mechanical clamps Something was do: Heavy docking clamps, open and empty. The wear marks outline a hull that looks familiar.
lines.The docking clamps are open, still holdi: The wear marks hold a scuffed outline I'd know anywhere: the Outrider was clamped here. Jettisoned, probably; the Choir don't leave getaway ships for specimens. I'm not leaving this way.
lines.The docking clamps are massive hydraulic: Massive hydraulic clamps. My hands barely fit round the smallest guide rail.
lines.Each clamp is bolted down with bolts thi: Bolted down with bolts thicker than my wrist. I leave them be.
lines.A locker containing alien emergency spac: A locker of alien emergency space suits, built for the crew.
lines.Emergency suit locker, cracked open from: A suit locker, cracked open. The suits are Choir-sized. I already have the helmet from Security, the only piece that fits.
lines.Emergency suit locker. Standard safety e: An emergency suit locker by the airlock. The suits are far too big for me. But the helmets...
lines.I pull the locker open. Three Choir emer: Three massive Choir suits, unwearable for me. But the helmets seal on their own. One might fit, like a bucket on my head.
lines.I pull the smallest helmet free. It's st: I pull out the smallest helmet. Too big, but the padding adjusts. It'll hold off vacuum, toxins and energy bursts, briefly.
lines.\"Emergency EVA equipment,\" I read from: "Emergency EVA equipment," I guess at the faded label. Every airlock in the galaxy says that.
lines.The panel hangs open, its override contr: The panel's open and glowing. The blast doors still lead only to vacuum, but the shutters over the great window answer to it too.
lines.I've already opened it. The controls hum: Already open. The controls hum under my fingers, waiting.
lines.A manual override panel for the airlock: An override panel under heavy bio-organic locks. The blast doors only lead to vacuum, and my ship's gone. But the circuitry might be good for something else.
lines.The locks are bio-organic and heavy, bui: Heavy bio-organic locks, built against accidental decompression. Bare hands won't do it.
lines.The key card slides home and the panel o: The key card slides home and the panel opens. I don't need the airlock, but one control is lit with a symbol I'd know anywhere: an eye. I press it. The armoured shutters over the great window fold back like a cathedral door.
lines.\"Come on, come on,\" I mutter at the pa: "Come on, come on." Its symbols glow politely, which is not the same as helping.
lines.Heavy organic-metallic blast doors seali: Heavy blast doors sealing the airlock.
lines.Massive blast doors designed to contain: Blast doors to the outer airlock, and beyond that, vacuum. Nothing out there but death. They're sealed for a reason.
lines.I press my palms against the blast doors: Sealed tight: inches of reinforced alloy between me and the airlock.
lines.\"These doors are the last barrier,\" I: "Last barrier," I say quietly. Beyond it: the airlock, then the void.
lines.A narrow ventilation opening near the fl: A narrow vent opening I could squeeze through.
lines.I climb back up through the hatch into t: I climb back up through the hatch into the vent exit passage.
lines.I duck down and squeeze back into the ve: I squeeze back into the shaft. The metal groans under me.
lines.The shaft behind me exhales stale, warm: The shaft breathes stale, warm air. Warmer than this bay, at least.
lines.I back away down the corridor before it: I back away before it turns around. Click. Click. Click. The sound follows me a long way.
Tall and thin, too many joints in its arms, two amber lenses for a face. It dips a long finger into my empty pod's fluid and tilts its head. It knows something is missing.
lines.Home. North America under a thin skin of: Home. North America under thin cloud, evening rolling in. Down there it's an ordinary Tuesday. And falling toward it from this ship, the siphon beams, drinking.
lines.Behind you, the clicking stops. You don': Behind you, the clicking stops. You don't turn around yet. You've seen what they're doing, and you know where you're going: down there, before the last of the eleven marks goes dark. The Harvest continues in Act 2.
lines.A small bio-organic jar from the process: A small bio-organic jar from the processing lab, now empty. Good for liquid samples.
lines.A small cylindrical jar made from the sa: A little jar of ship-stuff, seal broken but intact. It could hold a few ounces of liquid.
lines.The jar is lighter than glass and slight: Lighter than glass and slightly warm. It still smells of formaldehyde, or the alien equivalent.
lines.A vial of amber stasis fluid from my bro: A vial of amber stasis fluid from my broken pod, still faintly shimmering.
lines.The fluid is warm and viscous, with a fa: Warm, thick, faintly glowing amber. It kept me and hundreds of others under. Alien, but built to keep things alive.
lines.I swirl the vial gently. The fluid moves: I swirl it. It moves like honey and clings to the glass.
lines.Translucent and curved, still faintly st: Translucent, curved, stained amber, razor-edged. Some composite stronger and lighter than glass.
lines.I test the edge against my thumb. It dra: I test the edge on my thumb. Blood, immediately. Careful with this.
lines.An alien surgical instrument — curved bo: An alien surgical instrument: curved, bone-like, with a fine tip.
lines.It looks grown rather than manufactured:: Grown, not made: smooth bone tapering to a needle point. The grip's made for longer fingers, but it'll do.
lines.A bio-organic access card pulled from th: A bio-organic access card from the security hub. Pulses faintly.
lines.Not plastic — something closer to compre: Something like compressed cartilage laced with glowing circuits, pulsing like a heartbeat. Keyed to containment deck security.
lines.A small crystalline data storage device: A small data crystal from the specimen archive: a Choir officer's personal records.
lines.The crystal is the size of my thumb, fac: Thumb-sized and faceted, its light shifting as I tilt it. A Choir personal log, holding a fragment of a translation cipher. Piece one of four.
lines.Standard specimen feed. The tube is soft: Specimen feed, nutritionally complete for a dozen species and appetising to none. It could be bait: the drones are programmed to retrieve spilled feed.
lines.My own specimen identification tag from: My own specimen tag from the stasis pod. Proof of what I am to them.
lines.My own specimen tag. On the back, a ring: On the back, a ring of seven marks, six of them dark. A countdown, and I'm the last mark. I'd rather not see it go out.
lines.An alien emergency space helmet. Too lar: An alien emergency helmet. Too big for me, but it works.
lines.Designed for a Choir skull, far too larg: Made for a Choir skull, so it sits on me like a fishbowl, but the visor seals and the air system works. Good against vacuum and toxic air.
lines.The escapee's map, north at the top: the: North at the top: the Outer Ducts along the bottom, the Gut in the middle (east half torn off), the Purge Core on top. Circles are cold folds, rings breathing ducts, skulls purge ducts, bars grates. Nothing marks where I am.
lines.A section of neural interface tendril, s: A length of neural interface tendril, cut from an alien dormancy alcove.
lines.Rubbery, organic, about a foot long. The: Rubbery, a foot long, the cut end still sparking. The Choir plug these into their ship. With the right adapter, maybe I could too, if it can be fooled into taking human biology.
lines.The Choir vessel's flight recorder. Cont: The Choir vessel's flight recorder: the full mission log, including every world consumed.
lines.A dense, heavily shielded data device. I: Dense and heavily shielded: navigation logs, mission orders, specimen records, messages with the Convergence. Proof of what they've done, and what they're doing to the planet below.
lines.A Choir power cell from engineering. Com: A Choir power cell from engineering. Small, immensely powerful, warm.
lines.Bio-organic casing around a dense energy: A dense energy core in a bio-organic casing, humming and warm. One runs a Choir shuttle for weeks. Crack the casing and it lets go violently.
lines.A Choir tool repurposed as a weapon. Emi: A Choir tool turned weapon. Its subsonic pulse disrupts bio-mechanical systems.
lines.Not a weapon by design. It's a maintenan: A maintenance tool, really. Aimed at a bio-organic lock, it scrambles the resonance; aimed at a drone, it stalls it for a few seconds. Closest thing to a universal key.
lines.A crystalline navigation module from the: A crystal navigation module from the bridge: star charts and jump coordinates.
lines.A slim crystal wafer etched with navigat: A slim crystal wafer: star charts, jump coordinates, the Convergence's path across galaxies. Without it, no ship leaves this system; the jumps are too complex to work out by hand.
lines.A data pattern extracted from the Choir': A data pattern from the Choir's resonance chamber. The second piece of the translation key.
lines.Extracted from the communal resonance pa: Taken from the resonance patterns in the Choir's quarters. Their language is subsonic vibration, and this maps vibrations to meaning. With the other fragments, I could read their text.
lines.A crystal from the ship's data core that: A data-core crystal that resonates at the Choir's communication frequency.
lines.Deep purple, perfectly smooth, vibrating: Deep purple, perfectly smooth, humming at a pitch I feel in my teeth. Tuned to the Choir's network, the same frequency the Convergence uses to control its harvesters.
lines.A concentrated extract from the ship's h: A glowing, chemically complex extract from the ship's hydroponics bay.
lines.Harvested from the alien plants in the b: From the bio-garden's plants, glowing blue-green and dense with compounds. The Choir use it for food and neural repair. Combined right, it could bridge organic and crystalline systems.
lines.Technical diagrams of the ship's communi: Diagrams of the ship's communication array: frequencies, power and range.
lines.Detailed schematics showing the communic: Frequencies, power routing, targeting. With these, the array at the planet's nexus could be retuned to broadcast across the galaxy, if I could reach it.
lines.A replacement fuel conduit for the damag: A replacement fuel line for the damaged shuttle: organic tubing with self-sealing connectors.
lines.Bio-organic tubing that carries fuel fro: Bio-organic tubing whose connectors seal when pressed home. This, plus a power cell, gets the damaged shuttle flying.
lines.A sensory antenna pulled from a disabled: A sensory antenna from a disabled maintenance drone. Still picks up Choir signals.
lines.A thin, segmented antenna that twitches: Thin, segmented, twitching. Held to my ear, it picks up the Choir's distant clicks and hums. An early warning system.
lines.The flask is frosted on the outside — th: Frosted over; the coolant is near absolute zero. Crack the seal and out comes freezing vapour. For overheated systems, or anything organic in a pinch.
lines.Strong, flexible fiber harvested from al: Strong, flexible fibre from alien plants. Tougher than any rope.
lines.Harvested from the tendrils of the hydro: From the hydroponics tendrils; the Choir build and repair with it. It weaves, ties and wraps. With something sharp, it'd make a fine handle or binding.
lines.A distress beacon from the crashed shutt: A distress beacon from the crashed shuttle. Recalls any shuttle in range.
lines.A compact transmitter designed to recall: A transmitter that calls a shuttle to it, with range across the whole planet. If there's a working shuttle anywhere, this brings it. My ticket off this rock, if I want it.
lines.Crystalline mineral from the base of a s: A mineral crystal from the base of a siphon tower, holding Convergence energy.
lines.The soil near the siphon towers has been: Soil by the siphon towers, crystallised by the extraction. It holds a faint charge, and it resists energy flow rather than conducting it.
lines.A fragment broken from an energy siphon: A fragment broken off an energy siphon tower. Pulses with raw Convergence energy.
lines.It burns cold in my hand and crackles wi: It burns cold and crackles, still full of stolen planetary life. Very dangerous. Key to anything that has to touch Convergence energy systems.
lines.A personal journal from the refugee camp: A journal from the refugee camp, written by a four-armed scientist in the final days.
lines.The journal of Dr. Kaelith, a physicist: Dr. Kaelith's journal, a physicist who fled the city when the siphons began: the panic, the failed defences, the late evacuation. In the margins, cipher notation. Fragment three of four.
lines.A concentrated extract from the biolumin: An extract of the grove's glowing fungi. Purple in the dark.
lines.The fungi survived the Convergence's har: The fungi feed on the Convergence's leftover energy instead of being drained. The extract heals tissue and, with the right compounds, can suppress neural detection.
lines.Military-grade alien technology from the: Military tech from the bunker. Stabilises the field around Echoes so they're safe to approach.
lines.A handheld device that projects a stabil: A handheld stabilising field, built to study the Echoes: people trapped in the Convergence's energy. It calms them enough to interact with. Without it, getting near one is like standing in a lightning storm.
lines.A four-armed species' personal weapon. E: A four-armed species' sidearm. Energy-based, partly charged.
lines.Designed for a four-armed grip. I need b: Made for a four-armed grip; I need both hands. Maybe six shots left, each one deafening. Use it wisely, or not at all.
lines.Military blueprints showing the planet's: Military blueprints of the planet's defence against the Convergence.
lines.Detailed military plans for the planet's: Plans for a last stand: orbital defence satellites, ground weapons, and partial schematics of a weapon to disrupt the Convergence's energy. Incomplete, but they prove it was built.
lines.Vacuum-sealed packages of concentrated n: Vacuum-packed rations; the label shows a happy four-armed diner. Close enough for me. Eating one restores energy and clears my head.
lines.An emergency signal flare from the crash: An emergency signal flare from the Outrider's kit. Burns bright, burns loud.
lines.A human-made signal flare from the Outri: From the Outrider's emergency kit. Pull the cap and it burns blinding white for thirty seconds: a signal, a light, a distraction, or, wrapped right, a torch.
lines.Metal spikes from the refugee camp's sup: Metal spikes from the refugee camp's supplies, for climbing rock.
lines.Alien-made climbing aids: hardened metal: Hardened spikes with loops for rope; the refugees climbed the wasteland with them. For anything I can't reach on my own.
lines.A sensor badge from the bunker. Changes: A sensor badge from the bunker. Changes colour near dangerous Convergence energy.
lines.A simple but effective device — the crys: A crystal strip: green safe, yellow caution, red lethal. Soldiers used them near siphon towers. Near the nexus, it'll show the safe paths.
lines.An ornamental keystone from the grand pl: An ornamental keystone from the plaza's central statue. Opens restricted areas in the city.
lines.A crystalline key shaped like a miniatur: A crystal key shaped like a tiny four-armed figure: an administrator's master key, once set in the plaza statue. It opens government buildings, the war room and restricted infrastructure.
lines.The final fragment of the translation ci: The last fragment of the translation cipher, from the city library.
lines.The library's master index contained the: The last cipher fragment, from the library's master index: the city's key for its failed talks with the Choir. With all four, I can read any alien inscription.
lines.The heart of the civilization's counterm: The heart of the city's countermeasure weapon: a dense crystal sphere with energy pulsing inside.
lines.Heavy for its size — it feels like holdi: Like holding a small star. It resonates at the Convergence's own frequency, to turn its stolen energy on it. Inert alone; with the right parts, it can destroy the nexus.
lines.A command module for the planet's orbita: A command module for the planet's orbital defense satellites.
lines.The planet's last line of defense — a co: Most of its satellites are gone, but a few sleep in orbit. With enough power, they could make one devastating strike.
lines.A delicate locket from a residential hom: A delicate locket from a family home, with a holographic portrait inside.
lines.A small crystalline locket on a chain. I: A four-armed family of five, all smiling; the youngest holds a toy siphon tower. Carried near coherent Echoes, it sets off powerful reactions.
lines.An adapter that bridges the planet's tec: An adapter that bridges this planet's technology with alien power sources.
lines.The city's engineers designed this to in: Built to run the city's crystal systems off captured Choir power cells. A universal translator for machines.
lines.A sacred crystal from the temple. Shows: A sacred crystal from the temple. It shows possible futures to whoever holds it.
lines.The temple's priests used crystals like: The priests divined with these, and beat the odds. I see flashes: a nexus in flames, a signal to the stars, a frightened crystal mind, a small creature choosing.
lines.An access token for the city's undergrou: An access token for the city's underground railway.
lines.A small crystalline disc — a transit pas: A crystal pass that starts the city's rail cars, where the railway still has power. The tunnels also reach deeper passages under the city.
lines.A ceremonial tuning fork from the temple: A temple tuning fork. It hums at the old civilization's speaking frequency.
lines.The four-armed species communed through: They spoke by vibration. Combined with the Echo Stabilizer, this fork could let me truly talk with coherent Echoes.
lines.Protective eyewear from the research lab: Research-lab goggles that filter dangerous energy wavelengths.
lines.Oversized for my face but functional. Th: Too big for my face, but they filter the blinding light of Convergence systems, so I can look at high-energy areas and keep my eyes.
lines.Complete assembly instructions for the c: Assembly instructions for the countermeasure weapon, from the research lab.
lines.A holographic blueprint showing the comp: Three parts: a primed weapon core, an energy dampener and a siphon crystal fragment. Order matters: core first, dampener second, crystal last.
lines.Pure Convergence energy contained in a c: Pure Convergence energy in a crystal vial. Incredibly dangerous.
lines.The vial is cold enough to burn and brig: Cold enough to burn, bright enough to read by: a world's harvested life force. The vial barely holds it.
lines.A key from the Convergence's stasis gall: A key from the Convergence's stasis gallery. It opens the deepest parts of the nexus.
lines.Not Choir-made. Not from the planet's ci: Older than the Choir and this planet both: a crystal fractal that fits the oldest locks in the nexus.
lines.The Curator's personal communication dev: The Curator's own signal device. It can call the Choir vessel from orbit.
lines.Taken from — or given by — the Curator i: Keyed to the Curator's authority: it can recall the ship, command drones and override security.
lines.A module from the control spire that all: A control-spire module for a direct neural link with the Convergence intelligence.
lines.The Choir use these to receive instructi: The Choir take orders from the Convergence through these. Prepared right, any mind could link to it. Coming back is another matter.
lines.A mechanical key that opens the former c: A mechanical key to the old civilization's emergency escape shaft in the nexus.
lines.Found in the weapon assembly area, the f: It opens the shaft the old civilization carved up to the surface. My way out, if I take it.
The four-armed sidearm, fully charged with a Choir power cell.
Twenty shots instead of six. The grip was made for more hands than I have.
The complete translation cipher: all four fragments joined.
lines.I examine the complete translation ciphe: Every alien inscription is readable now. I used to struggle with flight-manual French.
The primed core inside its energy dampener.
One part left: the siphon crystal fragment.
The Echo Stabilizer with the temple tuning fork mounted in its emitter.
It carries my words to Echoes and brings their answers back clear.
A palm-sized blob of gel that drinks energy.
It soaks up power on contact and makes a dead zone near Convergence systems.
A flare wrapped in bio-fiber: a slow, steady torch.
It burns steady instead of blinding, and lasts far longer than the flare.
A paste that hides neural signatures.
Smeared on skin, it hides me from anything that senses energy, Echoes included. It smells as good as it sounds.
The defense grid controller, wired to the overcharge device.
Power for one devastating strike: the nexus, or the Choir ship.
A disruptor pulse amplified through a siphon crystal.
It can overload any energy system I aim it at. Once.
Two cipher fragments, interlocked: half the translation key.
Enough for simple alien text. Two fragments to go.
Three cipher fragments joined: most of the translation key.
I can read most operational text now. One fragment remains.
The weapon core, tuned with a Choir crystal and humming.
It hums at the Convergence's frequency. Next: the dampener, then the siphon crystal fragment.
The glass shard with a bio-fiber grip: a proper blade.
Stronger than tape. I can hold it without cutting myself, which is new.
Nutrient paste soaked in stasis fluid, now a deep amber.
The stuff that kept me asleep for days, concentrated. Touch it and sleep.
The helmet, lined with energy dampener gel.
With this on, the nexus's high-energy chambers won't fry my nerves.
It hums with the Convergence's own stolen energy. It kills planets. It can save them too.
The key card, rewritten by the disruptor: every access level at once.
It claims every clearance at once, and the doors seem to believe it.
The power adapter married to the navigation chip: a skeleton key for machines.
It can talk to anything: Choir, Convergence, or the old civilization's systems.
lines.A pre-recorded galactic broadcast signal: A recorded broadcast signal, ready to transmit to the galaxy.
lines.A carefully prepared broadcast signal co: Evidence of the harvest in one signal. Sent, it could warn every world in range.
lines.A device that creates a direct neural li: A device that links two minds directly.
lines.An alien neural bridge device. It could: An alien neural bridge. It could open a direct link to the Nexus consciousness.
lines.A Choir-make datapad recovered from a de: A Choir datapad from a dead crew member in the vents. Still faintly glowing.
lines.The datapad's screen shows the last entr: A Choir crewman's last log: a breach, the Curator sweeping the decks (crew too), a dash for the airlock through the vents. The last entry: coordinates, the ship's orbit over a blue world, and an override frequency for the operational decks.
lines.A small crystalline security chip from a: A small crystal security chip from a dead Choir crewman's uniform, still keyed to his clearance.
lines.A translucent chip the size of a thumbna: Veined with light, it broadcasts the holder's clearance to Choir locks, and the dead engineer's is still stored. It might fool a few doors.
lines.The chip is warm in my palm. The biolumi: The chip pulses faster in my palm, trying to read me. Wrong species, but the stored clearance may still open Choir systems.
lines.A long restraint strap cut from a proces: A long restraint strap cut from a processing-lab table. Tougher than any rope.
lines.Thick, leathery, unnervingly warm. Long: Thick, leathery and warm, strong enough to hold many times my weight. On its own, there's nothing to anchor it with.
lines.A barbed bio-metal hook from the morgue,: A barbed bio-metal hook from the morgue, for dragging bodies out of drawers.
lines.Heavy and curved like a talon, with a ba: Curved like a talon, with a backward barb and a thick eyelet. It would bite into any edge. Shame there's nothing tied to it.
lines.The strap is cinched through the hook's: The strap cinched through the hook's eyelet with the best knot I know. Throw it, let the barb bite, and it'll take my weight.
lines.A plain gold band. Engraved inside, worn: Engraved inside, worn almost smooth: 'M & J. Always.' No use to me at all, and the most human thing on this ship.
lines.A plump, translucent sac, veined with am: A plump amber-veined sac tied off with sinew. It holds four breaths: squeeze it (the button up top) to breathe anywhere. Folds and air rooms refill it.
lines.A hollow shell pierced with breathing ho: A hollow shell with breathing holes. Tap it on a grate and the colony knocks on the walls far away.
lines.A palm-sized oval of dark shell, hollow,: Tapped on a grate in the Core, it sets the colony knocking far off and draws the Curator away. Two taps; they come back if I start the Core again.
lines.My specimen tag, riddled with bore holes: Riddled with bore holes, its display dark. The brood ate the signal and the countdown with it. It still says what I am, just not where.
lines.One egg of the colony, in a cradle of si: One of the colony's eggs, in a cradle of sinew. A gift for someone she calls kin.
lines.A hen's-egg-sized sac of glowing amber,: A hen's-egg-sized sac of glowing amber with a curled larva inside. It's warm, and now and then it breathes.
lines.One of the Keth-Vari's own claws, bent i: One of the Keth-Vari's own claws, wired into a loop and scratched with tally marks. It fits. A promise in a language I'm still learning.
lines.A round patch, faded orange around a sti: Faded orange, a rocket in a ring of stars. On the back in marker: V. HALLORAN, LIFE SUPPORT. I'll take her name home.
lines.A Choir maintenance tool from the Cache:: From the Cache: a long bone-handled rod with a dozen folding prongs. Long and strong enough to jam a fan.
lines.The last of the stasis fluid drains from: The last of the fluid drains from my pod, and I shiver. Around me, other pods glow. A few of their occupants are moving.
lines.Click. Click. Click. Somewhere far below: Click. Click. Click. Far below, precise footsteps on grating. The Curator is making its rounds.
lines.A pod near me rattles. Something inside: A nearby pod rattles. The thing inside opens its eyes, unfocused, and closes them. Not all the specimens are dead.
lines.The ship pulses. The bioluminescent vein: The veins in the walls brighten, then fade, like a heartbeat. I get the feeling the ship just noticed something.
lines.A change in the ship's resonance. The Cu: The ship's hum changes. The Curator has found signs of me, and its amber light sweeps faster.
lines.A new sound: the skittering of small mec: Small legs skitter: spider-like maintenance drones fan out. The Curator has sent its helpers.
lines.The viewport shows the planet in full. E: Siphons stab down from orbit, and where they touch, the land blackens. I'm watching a murder from the killer's house.
lines.Smoke rises from the shuttle wreckage be: The shuttle wreck smokes behind me; that beetle won't fly again. I'm alone on a dying world.
lines.Reality stutters. A translucent figure m: Reality stutters. A see-through, four-armed figure walks three steps, turns and walks back, over and over. An Echo: one of this world's dead, burned into the Convergence's field.
lines.Collapsed shelters. Scattered belongings: Collapsed shelters, a barricade, and tall four-armed skeletons behind it. They didn't make it out.
lines.Something new. A geometric shape — a shi: A shifting polyhedron of light drifts between the spires. It doesn't move; it optimizes. The Watcher.
lines.The room splits. Half decayed ruin, half: The room splits: half ruin, half living city. Through the Echo Stabilizer, a ghostly scientist: '...the weapon core must be shielded before assembly or the energy will...' Then it fractures.
lines.The nexus surges. Energy flows brighten,: The nexus surges and the hum rises to a roar. The harvest is speeding up; the planet is running out of time.
lines.A distant boom. A Choir shuttle crashes: A boom: a Choir shuttle crashes near the nexus entrance, and amber light climbs out. The Curator crashed a ship to chase one specimen. I'm almost flattered.
lines.It speaks. Not in words: in visions. Con: It speaks in visions: oceans turned to dust, thousands of worlds reduced to Echoes. Under it all, the Convergence is afraid. The universe is winding down, and it eats to survive.
lines.The visions fade. I'm standing before so: The visions fade. Something older than most stars has shown me its fear. Now it wants my answer.
lines.A gallery of the damned. Specimens from: The Convergence's first specimens, each the last of its kind, sealed in crystal. Among them, one of this world's four-armed people, mid-scream. They got this far.
lines.The sky darkens further. The energy siph: The sky darkens and the planet shudders. The siphons are near their limit. I'd better hurry.
lines.Somewhere above me, the clicking footste: Somewhere above, the clicking footsteps stop. Something is listening. (I'm making too much noise.)
lines.Click. Click. Click. Closer now, and qui: Click. Click. Click. Closer, quicker. The Curator is hunting the noise. I need to hide and keep still until it passes.
lines.The clicking stops right behind you. Lon: The clicking stops right behind you, and cold fingers close on your shoulders. The Curator carries you home and seals the pod this time. Keep the noise down, and hide when it hunts.
lines.Click. Click. Click. From back the way I: Click. Click. Click. From back the way I came. I flatten against the doorway and look toward the stasis hold. Something is standing over my empty pod.
lines.The alarm is everywhere now. With a hiss: The alarm is everywhere. With a hiss and a clang, the floor grate lurches off its bolts and red light pours up from the shaft. Behind these doors, something fast is clicking. The vent, now.
lines.A hunter drone is drifting between the p: A hunter drone drifts between the pods, lens sweeping. It finds me before the door has finished opening.
A hunter drone finds you before the door finishes opening. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)
lines.Two lenses turn toward the doorway at on: Two lenses turn to the doorway at once. The lab is full of hunters, and they were waiting for this.
The lab was full of hunters, waiting for exactly this. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)
lines.I go back for one last look. So does the: I go back for one last look. So does the hunter drone already hovering over the console.
lines.You go back for one last look. So does t: You went back for one last look, and so did the hunter drone. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)
lines.Something is already bent over the open: Something is bent over the open drawers, sorting. A hunter drone lifts from the slab and turns its lens on me.
A hunter drone was sorting the morgue drawers. It sorted you. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)
lines.The hologram is still spinning. In its l: In the spinning hologram's light, a hunter drone drifts between the shelves. It's already seen me.
In the hologram's light, a hunter drone saw you first. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)
lines.Above you the grate goes dark. An eye fi: The grate above goes dark. A vast wet eye fills it, and a voice like a chord says: "Let the walls have it." The clicking upstairs stops. They've left me to the vents.
lines.Scratched into the ledge, fresh: a map o: Scratched into the ledge, fresh: a map of the torn half of the Gut, in four-fingered strokes. Someone wants me to have it. The Keth-Vari hasn't forgiven me.
lines.Far off down the Core, a shriek: four-ar: Far down the Core, a shriek, furious and deliberate. The hum behind the walls swings toward it. The Keth-Vari has bought me some room.
lines.From the duct behind you, a shriek, righ: A shriek from the duct behind me, right by the grate: the Keth-Vari, calling the Curator to me. The hum turns my way.
lines.Through the walls, all across the Gut, t: All across the Gut, the colony breathes in at once. The Wardens stop hunting, the membranes stay open, and new ducts appear on my map in four-fingered scratches.
lines.Containment locks disengage throughout t: Containment locks let go and new corridors open. The Curator's patrol has changed. It knows something's wrong.
lines.The architecture shifts from clinical to: The walls turn alien, carved with geometric patterns, and the air tastes alive. This is where the Choir live.
lines.The shuttle's systems initialize. The ba: The bay door opens on stars and the planet below, but amber light sweeps the bay. I have seconds to launch.
lines.The shuttle hits the ground hard. I craw: The shuttle hits hard. Grey soil, trees frozen in crystal, beams draining the planet, a city in the distance. Off the ship, but not free.
lines.The city gates loom above me, massive, e: The half-collapsed city gates are carved with four-armed figures. Beyond, lights still burn in some windows. Something moved in there.
lines.I step into the dead city. Everything is: Everything here stopped mid-moment: a meal on a table, toys on a floor. The Echoes are stronger, and a shape of light drifts between the spires. The Convergence knows I'm here.
lines.The weapon vault opens. They built somet: The weapon vault opens. They nearly finished a weapon against the Convergence; its parts are scattered through the containment units. The Watcher's patrols tighten.
The nexus walls are crystallized energy, and stolen life flows past me toward the core. It all comes down to what happens next.
lines.The core. A crystalline intelligence fil: A fractal crystal mind fills the chamber, flooding me with visions of consumed worlds and a dying universe. It is afraid, it is merciless, and it is waiting for my choice.
lines.A low hum and the tick of jointed legs,: A low hum and the tick of jointed legs. Something is coming this way.
lines.A hum and a fast tick of metal legs from: A hum and fast-ticking legs from the far side of the hold: a hunter drone on its rounds, coming this way. Get out of its way, or back into your pod.
lines.From the Stasis Hold, the hum of a hunte: From the Stasis Hold, a hunter drone's hum and the tick of its legs along the walkway.
lines.Out in the corridor, metal legs tick pas: Out in the corridor, metal legs tick past the door: a hunter drone on its rounds. Stay put until it's gone.
lines.The hunter drone, ticking along the corr: The hunter drone is ticking along the corridor towards you. Get out of its path.
The hunter drone is at the archive door. Nowhere to run in here: hide.
lines.The hunter drone stops dead. Its eye swi:
The drone's eye turns from amber to red. It pins you and hums until the Curator collects you.

The drones sweep these rooms every minute, and you can hear them coming. Watch the clock, leave the room, or hide.
lines.Clicking, getting closer, and the air mo: Clicking, closer, and the air moves the wrong way: a Warden is coming down this duct. Get into a cold fold, or out of its way.
lines.Somewhere close, through the flesh of th: Close by, through the wall: a dry clicking, moving along the ducts.
lines.It stops. Its head swings toward you, sl: It stops. Its head swings my way, slits flaring, tasting my breath.
lines.The Wardens hunt anything the colony doe: Wardens see by moving air and hunt anything the colony doesn't know. They loop on a rhythm and you hear them coming: get into a cold fold (HAND it) or out of their way. Once the Queen accepts you, they'll let you pass.
lines.A deep roar from the north, and every du: A deep roar from the north, every duct breathes out, and the Vesk scramble for the folds. A purge surge is coming: into a cold fold, or out of the north ducts, now.
The hot wind arrives. It isn't wind.
lines.The Purge Core's surge overflows the bor: Every few minutes the Purge Core's surge spills over the border along the Gut's north ducts. You get six seconds of warning: the roar, and the Vesk running for folds. Hide in a cold fold, or get south of the north rows.
lines.It turns. A click, then the whole city a: It turns. A click, and the whole city answers.
lines.The Vesk see by moving air. On the lung': The Vesk feel moving air. On the in-breath the wind hides you; in the still, anything moving near a Warden is felt. Walk with the wind, freeze in the still, use the pillar and alcove shadows. You start again from the ledge.
lines.A low hum, right behind the grate. Somet: A low hum, right behind the grate. Something very large has stopped on the other side. Leave, or hold your breath, NOW.
lines.Behind you a long grey hand gropes throu: A long grey hand gropes through the grate into an empty duct and withdraws. The hum moves off down the wall.
lines.Your chest is starting to burn. Find air: Your chest is burning. Find air soon: a cold fold, a room with air, or a breathing duct on its in-breath.
Your heart is pounding in your ears. One breath left.
lines.You blacked out. The Gut's air is thin b: You blacked out. The colony breathes most of the Gut's air, so every screen costs a breath. Plan fold to fold, LISTEN for cold air (one breath, but it tells you where), and take breathing ducts on the in-breath.
lines.The hum behind the walls is very loud no: The hum behind the walls is very loud and the heat seams are white. Two more moves.
lines.The Curator reached the controls first a: The Curator reached the controls first and fired the purge. The race always starts the same: from where it turns, take the shortest way to the Purge Heart (count it on your map) and jam it with the probe or the Choir multitool.
lines.You press the four characters from the s: I press the four characters from the specimen displays, in order. ACCESS GRANTED. Red script crawls past two symbols I know: the cross from the dead button on the security console, and a hand pressing down. The override is armed. It wants a hand on that button in Security.
The keypad flushes crimson and shrieks. A ceiling hatch snaps open and a hunter drone unfolds, gliding toward the terminal. I back away fast.
lines.The resonance tones harmonize. The bridg: The tones harmonize and star maps bloom over the bridge console. Hundreds of systems, most marked red. Consumed.
lines.The reactor's heartbeat shifts rhythm. P: The reactor changes rhythm and power surges to the shuttle bay. The alarms stay quiet. For now.
lines.An alarm blares briefly before the syste: An alarm blares, then the system compensates. Wrong configuration.
lines.Static resolves into something alien — s: Subsonic pulses I can't read, but the recorder can: the black box starts logging the Convergence's coordinates and orders.
lines.A burst of static. Wrong frequency — the: A burst of static. Wrong frequency; the array whines.
lines.The blast door groans open for the first: The blast door groans open for the first time in decades, and amber emergency strips light the dust. Someone built this to last.
lines.The dials click but the door holds. Wron: The dials click, but the door holds. Wrong combination.
lines.The crystals dim and reset. A discordant: The crystals dim and reset with a discordant tone.
lines.The crystals align in harmonic resonance: The crystals align, and centuries of research on the Convergence flood the station, weaknesses included. Among the records: the fourth cipher fragment.
lines.Generators hum to life. Lights flicker o: Lights come on in the chosen districts. Somewhere in the ruins, the Watcher takes notice.
lines.Overload. The grid sparks and resets. To: Overload. The grid sparks and resets. Too many districts for the power left.
lines.The resonance chamber thrums with ancien: The murals glow and a crystal rises from the altar, full of futures: a weapon assembled, a bridge between minds, an escape into darkness, a warning sent to the stars. I'm in all of them.
lines.The chamber responds with a mournful dro: The chamber answers with a mournful drone. Wrong frequency.
lines.Seven tones lock into ancient harmony. T: Seven tones lock into harmony and the ancient controls light up. From here, the harvest can be redirected, stopped or overloaded.
lines.The Convergence-era lock rejects the com: The ancient lock rejects the combination with a crystalline screech.
lines.The crystalline antenna vibrates at a fr: The antenna hums in my teeth. Galactic sweep engaged: every inhabited system in range will hear it.
lines.She is quiet. She heard you. Then the br: She's quiet. She heard me. Then the brood rustle, and the air fills with my smell, and under it something Choir.
lines.The brood hiss and the guard shoulders y: The brood hiss and the guard shoulders me back up into the brood chamber. Nothing is lost. Go down and try again.
lines.You thread the strap through the hook's: I thread the strap through the hook's eyelet, cinch it and haul with all my weight. It holds: a grappling line.
lines.You wrap the bio-fiber tightly around th: I wrap the bio-fiber around the base of the glass shard. It bonds to the glass, stronger than tape. A proper blade now.
lines.You mix the nutrient paste with the stas: Paste and stasis fluid turn deep amber: the stuff that kept me asleep for days, smearable. Touch it and sleep.
lines.You pulse the disruptor through the key: I pulse the disruptor through the key card's bio-circuits. It now claims every access level at once.
lines.The mineral dissolves into the stasis fl: The mineral sets in the stasis fluid into a gel that drinks power on contact: a dead zone near Convergence systems.
lines.You channel the disruptor's pulse throug: The siphon crystal amplifies the disruptor a hundredfold: one burst that can overload any energy system. One shot.
lines.The fungal extract reacts with the sedat: Fungal extract and sedative make a paste that hides me from anything that senses energy, Echoes included.
lines.You align the two cipher fragments. The: The two fragments interlock: half the cipher. Simple alien text only, for now. Two fragments to go.
lines.The refugee journal's margin notations c: The journal's margin notes add a third fragment. I can read most operational text now. One remains.
lines.The final fragment locks into place. The: The last fragment locks in, and every inscription, label and record is readable. Like remembering a language I forgot.
lines.You press the Choir crystal against the: I press the Choir crystal to the weapon core and it hums at the Convergence's frequency. Primed. Next: the dampener, then the siphon crystal fragment.
lines.The adapter accepts the navigation chip': The adapter bridges the navigation chip to a universal power bus: a skeleton key for any machine.
lines.You wire the overcharge device into the: I wire the overcharge device into the defense grid controller: power for one strike, at the nexus or the Choir ship.
lines.You wrap the bio-fiber around the flare': Bio-fiber around the flare's head: it burns slow and steady, a torch that far outlasts the flare.
lines.You line the helmet's interior with the: I line the helmet with dampener gel. Now the nexus's high-energy chambers won't fry my nerves.
lines.You mount the tuning fork in the stabili: With the tuning fork in its emitter, the stabilizer carries my words to Echoes and brings their answers back clear.
lines.The Choir power cell slots into the alie: The Choir power cell slots in and the sidearm hums. Twenty shots instead of six. The four-armed grip is awkward.
lines.The energy dampener wraps around the pri: The dampener wraps the primed core. One more part, the siphon crystal fragment, and the countermeasure is done.
lines.The siphon crystal fragment snaps into t: The siphon crystal fragment snaps in, and the countermeasure wakes, humming with stolen energy. It kills planets. It can save them too.
lines.You hold your breath and listen. Only th: I hold my breath and listen. Only the ship breathing. Nothing near.
I squeeze the lung-sac and breathe.
